posts.title: Play & Compete: Sports in Hatfield
posts.content:
Hatfield is bursting with opportunities to get active, meet new people, and have fun along the way. Whether you're a competitive athlete, a weekend warrior, or simply looking for a gentle way to move more, this vibrant Hertfordshire town has something for everyone. From team sports and fitness classes to scenic outdoor trails and family-friendly fun, here's your guide to playing and competing in Hatfield.

Team Sports for Every Level

Hatfield is home to a range of local clubs and community leagues covering popular team sports such as football, rugby, netball, cricket, and hockey. Many clubs welcome players of all abilities, from complete beginners to seasoned competitors, and often run mixed, men's, women's, and junior sections. Joining a team is a brilliant way to build fitness, make friends, and become part of the local sporting community. Check with local sports centres, community noticeboards, and social media groups for current team listings, training sessions, and how to get involved.

Individual Fitness and Recreation

Prefer to set your own pace? Hatfield offers a variety of options for individual fitness, including gyms, leisure centres with swimming pools, group exercise classes, and studios offering yoga, pilates, and strength training. Many facilities offer flexible membership options and drop-in sessions, so you can find a routine that fits your lifestyle. Personal trainers and fitness instructors across the area can also help tailor a programme to your goals, whatever your current fitness level.

Outdoor Activities and Green Spaces

Hatfield's parks, green spaces, and countryside trails make it easy to combine exercise with fresh air and nature. Enjoy walking or jogging routes through local parks, cycle along dedicated paths and quiet lanes, or try your hand at outdoor activities like tennis, bowls, or disc golf at community facilities. Nearby waterways and open spaces also offer opportunities for rowing, paddleboarding, or simply a peaceful countryside stroll. These outdoor options are perfect for all ages and fitness levels, and many are free or low-cost to enjoy.

Family-Friendly Options

Getting active as a family has never been easier in Hatfield. Look out for junior sports clubs, holiday activity camps, and family swim sessions at local leisure centres. Many parks feature playgrounds, outdoor gyms, and open fields ideal for kickabouts or picnics with a side of frisbee. Soft play centres and family fun days also offer a great way for younger children to burn off energy while parents stay active too. These options are a wonderful way to build healthy habits together as a family.

Practical Tips for Getting Involved

  • Check local community centres, leisure facilities, and council websites for up-to-date class timetables, membership details, and pricing before you go.
  • Follow local sports clubs and groups on social media to stay informed about taster sessions, new member drives, and upcoming events.
  • Many clubs offer a free or discounted trial session, so don't be afraid to turn up and try something new.
  • Bring suitable footwear and clothing for outdoor activities, and always check the weather forecast ahead of time.
  • Consider activities with a friend or family member, it's a great way to stay motivated and accountable.
  • If you're unsure where to start, speak with staff at your local leisure centre, who can point you toward activities suited to your fitness level and interests.

Ready to Get Moving?

Whatever your age, ability, or interest, Hatfield has a sport or activity waiting for you. There's no better time than now to lace up your trainers, grab a teammate, or simply step outside and start moving. Explore what's on offer, find the activity that excites you, and take that first step toward a healthier, more active lifestyle today.

Explore More Healthy Activities

posts.title: Play and Compete: Affordable Sports
posts.content:
Staying active in St Albans does not have to be expensive. From community sessions and open-air spaces to simple ways of exercising with friends, there are plenty of flexible options for different ages, abilities, and budgets. Children may enjoy playful games and short bursts of activity, adults might prefer structured classes or social sports, and older people may benefit from gentler options such as walking groups or low-impact classes. Whatever you choose, check what is suitable for your fitness level, any health conditions, and your confidence, and speak to a health professional if you are unsure. Availability and costs change, so always check current information from the local council, leisure centres, and sports clubs before you go, and look for clear details on opening times, booking arrangements, and any extra charges.

Low-cost community sports

Community sports sessions can be a welcoming way to try something new without committing to expensive equipment or long memberships. Look for local programmes, coached taster sessions, social groups, and activities delivered through community venues that match your age, ability, and interests. Many sessions are designed for beginners or specific groups, such as families, young people, or older adults, so ask which option is right for you. Ask about concessions, pay-as-you-go options, and introductory sessions, and confirm the latest details on times, booking requirements, and costs before attending. Going along with a friend, neighbour, or family member can make it easier to join in, and you can support each other to keep going.

Parks and outdoor courts

Parks and public outdoor spaces can make exercise simple and affordable. Walking, fitness circuits, informal games, and bodyweight exercises need little or no specialist kit and can be adapted for different ages and abilities. Families can use play areas for active games, adults can walk, jog, or stretch, and older people may prefer steady walks on even paths or benches for gentle exercises. Use local parks respectfully: keep to paths where requested, share space with other users, follow signs, take litter home, and avoid causing damage or noise at unsociable hours. Outdoor courts may also be useful for basketball, tennis, or other casual activities; check whether a space requires booking, has access restrictions, or is shared at busy times, and confirm any rules about lighting, opening hours, and acceptable footwear or equipment.

Casual football and group games

Casual football is an easy way to combine exercise and social time. A small group can organise a friendly game in a suitable park or book an available pitch when needed, choosing a format that matches everyone’s age, fitness, and experience. Keep games short and flexible for younger children, allow regular breaks, and agree simple rules so play stays safe and enjoyable for all. Sharing the cost of a booking, rotating equipment, and joining an open community session can help keep participation affordable, especially for regular games. Bring suitable footwear, plenty of water, and weather-appropriate clothing, and always check local rules, pitch conditions, and current availability first so that your game is safe, permitted, and fully booked if required.

Running and walking

Running and brisk walking are among the lowest-cost ways to get active. Start with short, comfortable outings and build gradually, or use a walk-run approach if you are new to running, adjusting the pace to your age, fitness, and any health conditions. Children may prefer short, playful bursts of running, adults can use timed intervals, and older people may favour steady walks with occasional brisk sections. Warm up safely with a few minutes of gentle walking and easy movements for your joints before increasing the pace, and finish with slower walking and light stretches. Parks, pavements, and quiet routes can all work, but choose well-lit places, consider how busy they are, and be considerate of other path users. Check local guidance about routes, surfaces, and conditions, and wear comfortable shoes, weather-appropriate clothing, and anything else you need to feel safe and visible.

Cycling around St Albans

Cycling can be both exercise and a practical way to explore the area. Riding a bike you already own, borrowing one, or sharing basic maintenance with friends can reduce costs, and family members can sometimes swap bikes as children grow. Plan a route that suits your confidence, fitness, and type of bike, starting with quieter paths or shorter loops if you are less experienced or cycling with children. Wear appropriate safety equipment, such as a well-fitted helmet if you use one, and consider lights and reflective gear so that you can be seen clearly. Check the condition of your cycle before setting off, including tyres, brakes, and chain, and carry simple items such as water, a small snack, and basic tools if you know how to use them. Look up local guidance on cycling routes, shared paths, and any access rules so that you use roads and off-road areas safely and respectfully.

Swimming and indoor activities

Swimming is a useful full-body activity and can suit people who prefer lower-impact exercise. It can be particularly helpful for those with joint issues or who find weight-bearing activities uncomfortable, though you should seek professional advice if you have specific health concerns. Leisure centres may offer different session types, such as lane swimming, family sessions, and beginner classes, as well as memberships, concessions, or casual entry arrangements. Choose a session that fits your confidence, swimming ability, and age group, and ask about quieter times if you prefer a less busy environment. Bring suitable swimwear, a towel, and any aids you use, and check current timetables, access information, and booking requirements directly with the centre. If you need step-free access, pool hoists, or accessible changing, ask about these in advance so you can plan your visit and feel comfortable on arrival.

Beginner-friendly ways to get started

If you are starting from scratch, choose an activity that feels manageable and enjoyable. A short walk, gentle cycle, beginner class, or relaxed game is enough to begin, and you can adapt the intensity to your age, fitness level, and any health conditions. Warm up with a few minutes of light movement before doing anything more energetic, and stop or slow down if you feel unwell, overly breathless, or in pain. Invite a friend or family member to join you, set a small weekly goal, and increase time or intensity slowly so your body can adjust. Think about what you might need to bring, such as comfortable clothing, supportive footwear, water, a light snack, or any medication you usually carry. If you have health concerns or have not exercised for a while, seek appropriate professional advice before making a big change to your routine.

Practical ways to keep costs down

Use free public spaces where suitable, borrow or share equipment, and look after what you already own so it lasts longer. Compare pay-as-you-go sessions with memberships, ask about concessions or community discounts, and choose activities that do not require specialist clothing, especially when you are just starting out. Before attending, check whether you need to book in advance, how long sessions last, and whether there are different prices for adults, children, older people, or people on certain incomes. If accessibility is important to you, ask about step-free access, changing facilities, toilets, parking, or support for people with additional needs so that you can take part comfortably and safely. Planning ahead can also prevent unnecessary travel and last-minute booking costs. Current offers and rules vary, so confirm details with the relevant council, leisure centre, or club, and make a note of any changes to opening times or prices over holidays or special events.

Check current local information

Local facilities, programmes, opening times, booking arrangements, and prices can change. Before setting out, check the latest information from St Albans City and District Council, nearby leisure centres, and local sports clubs or community organisations, including whether you need to book, how to pay, and what to bring. If you have specific needs around accessibility, age, ability level, or health conditions, ask clearly about these so you can choose a suitable activity and avoid surprises on arrival. That way, you can find an option that is affordable, appropriate for your level, and available when you need it. Take a moment now to pick one low-cost activity that feels realistic for you this week, make a simple plan, and give yourself credit for taking that first step.

posts.title: Family Fitness and Affordable Sports in Welwyn Garden City Parks
posts.content:
Play and Compete: Affordable Sports in Welwyn Garden City

Whether you're a longtime resident or just visiting, Welwyn Garden City offers plenty of ways to stay active without spending a fortune. From green parks to community clubs and leisure centres, there's something for every budget and interest. This guide walks you through the options so you can find your next game, run, or workout.

Parks and Outdoor Spaces

Welwyn Garden City's design as a garden city means green spaces are woven throughout the town. Local parks offer open fields, walking paths, and informal areas where you can play football, practice yoga, or simply enjoy fresh air. These spaces are free to use and ideal for casual games with friends or family, making them a great starting point for low-cost activity.

When choosing a park or open space, think about what you want to do there. A flat, well-maintained field suits informal football or rounders, while a looped path with a firm, even surface is better for jogging or a brisk walk. If you're planning an outdoor workout, look for areas with some open grass or firm ground for stretching and bodyweight exercises, and ideally a bit of shade for warmer days. Spaces with clear sightlines and some footfall from other visitors tend to feel safer and more comfortable, especially if you're exercising alone or early or late in the day. Visiting a few different spots at different times can help you find the ones that best match your routine.

Community Sports Clubs

The town is home to a variety of community sports clubs covering disciplines such as football, rugby, cricket, tennis, and bowls. Joining a local club is often more affordable than private coaching and comes with the added benefit of meeting like-minded people. Many clubs welcome newcomers of all skill levels and offer taster sessions, so it's worth reaching out directly to ask about joining fees and training schedules.

When comparing clubs, ask about the structure of a typical session, including how much time is spent on coaching versus free play, and whether sessions are organised by age or ability. Find out whether the club offers a trial or taster session so you can get a feel for the coaching style and the other members before committing. It's also worth asking about group sizes, how equipment is provided or shared, and whether the club has any affiliations with national governing bodies, which can be a useful marker of consistent standards. Finally, consider the practicalities: how easy the venue is to reach, whether parking or public transport works for your schedule, and how flexible the club is if your availability changes.

Leisure-Centre Activities

Local leisure centres provide swimming pools, gyms, and group fitness classes under one roof. Many offer pay-as-you-go options alongside memberships, so you can choose what suits your budget and how often you plan to visit. Checking for off-peak sessions or introductory offers directly with the centre can help you get the most value.

To keep leisure centre visits affordable, start by comparing pay-as-you-go rates against membership options based on how often you realistically expect to visit. Many centres offer discounted rates for off-peak times, so shifting your visit outside the busiest hours can make a noticeable difference. Look out for short-term passes or trial periods if you're not ready to commit to a longer membership, and ask whether concessions are available for students, families, or other groups. Combining activities, such as a swim and a gym session in one visit, can also help you get more value from a single admission.

Running and Cycling

With its network of parks, green corridors, and quiet residential streets, Welwyn Garden City is well suited to running and cycling. These activities require little more than suitable footwear or a bike, making them some of the most cost-effective ways to stay fit. Local running groups and cycling clubs can also provide motivation, routes, and a sense of community for those who prefer not to go it alone.

Good habits make running and cycling both safer and more enjoyable. Warm up gradually, stick to routes you know well until you're confident navigating busier junctions or shared paths, and wear clothing that keeps you visible, particularly in low light. Carrying water on longer outings and pacing yourself according to the terrain and weather will help you avoid overexertion. For cycling, a well-fitted helmet, working lights, and a quick pre-ride check of brakes and tyres are simple steps that reduce risk. Whichever you choose, varying your routes keeps things interesting and helps you discover more of the town's green corridors and quieter streets.

Family-Friendly Options

Families looking to stay active together have plenty of choices, from playgrounds and open parkland to family swim sessions and junior sports clubs. Many clubs and centres offer sibling or family rates, so it's worth asking about group discounts when you enquire. Outdoor play areas remain a free and flexible option for younger children on any day of the week.

For a successful active family day, plan around the shortest attention span in the group and build in plenty of breaks and snacks. Mixing a free activity, such as time at a playground or open parkland, with a paid one, like a family swim session, can balance cost with variety. Letting older children help choose the activity often increases enthusiasm, and packing simple equipment like a ball or skipping rope means you're never short of something to do. Keeping plans flexible also means you can adapt quickly if the weather changes or energy levels dip.

Practical Ways to Keep Costs Low

  • Take advantage of free outdoor spaces for running, walking, and casual games.
  • Ask local clubs about taster sessions before committing to membership.
  • Compare pay-as-you-go versus membership rates at leisure centres to match your usage.
  • Look out for off-peak or introductory offers at local facilities.
  • Check for family or group discounts when signing up with others.
  • Borrow or share equipment where possible to avoid upfront costs.

With a little planning, staying active in Welwyn Garden City can fit comfortably into almost any budget. From free parkland to welcoming clubs and flexible leisure-centre options, residents and visitors alike have plenty of ways to play, compete, and keep moving.

Conclusion

Staying active in Welwyn Garden City doesn't have to come with a high price tag. By making the most of free green spaces, comparing your options at local clubs and leisure centres, and building safe, sustainable habits into your running, cycling, and family time, you can create a routine that fits your budget and your lifestyle. A little research and a willingness to try a few different options go a long way toward finding what works best for you.

posts.title: Visit St Albans City Football Club: Family-Friendly Days at Clarence Park
posts.content:
Matchday in Herts: A Closer Look at St Albans City Football Club

A Heritage Built Over Generations

Few institutions capture the spirit of a town quite like its local football club, and St Albans City is no exception. Founded well over a century ago, the club has become a thread running through the city's social history, with generations of families passing down their support from one to the next. Long before the modern era of elite football dominated headlines, clubs like this one were the beating heart of weekend life in towns across England, and that tradition continues today.

Visiting the club isn't just about watching a game — it's a small window into the living history of St Albans itself, where the rhythms of matchday have shaped community life for decades.

Clarence Park: A Historic Home Ground

St Albans City play their home matches at Clarence Park, a charming and historic ground that sits within a public park setting rather than a modern stadium complex. This gives the venue a distinctive character you won't find at bigger clubs — open green space surrounds the pitch, mature trees line the boundary, and the whole experience feels woven into the everyday fabric of the city rather than cordoned off from it.

The park setting also means Clarence Park doubles as a pleasant green space in its own right, popular for walks and leisurely visits even outside of matchdays, which only adds to its appeal as a community landmark.

Family and Community Appeal

One of the biggest draws of a visit to St Albans City is how welcoming and family-friendly the whole experience tends to be. Unlike large-scale professional fixtures, non-league football at this level is typically relaxed, affordable, and easy to navigate with children in tow. Grounds like Clarence Park tend to have a calm, sociable pace — ideal for introducing younger family members to live football for the first time without the overwhelming crowds or costs associated with top-flight games.

It's also a great opportunity to meet other local families and long-time supporters, many of whom are happy to chat with newcomers and share their own matchday traditions — a reminder that community football is as much about connection as it is about the final score.

Planning Your Visit

  • Check the club's official website or social media channels closer to the date for current fixtures, kick-off times, and ticket information, as these can change throughout the season.
  • Dress for the outdoors — as an open park ground, Clarence Park offers little shelter from the elements, so bring layers and weather-appropriate clothing.
  • Arrive with time to spare to enjoy the surrounding park atmosphere and find a comfortable spot before kick-off.
  • Consider combining your visit with a wider stroll around Clarence Park, making it an easy half-day outing for the whole family.
  • Public transport and local parking options around St Albans are worth checking in advance, particularly on busier matchdays.

Location: Clarence Park

Clarence Park, York Road, St Albans, Hertfordshire, AL1 4PL, United Kingdom.

  • Clarence Park

If you're looking for a brilliant way to spend a weekend afternoon in Hertfordshire, you don't need to look far. St Albans City Football Club offers a proper slice of grassroots football culture, right on our doorstep. Whether you're a lifelong supporter, a curious newcomer, or simply searching for a fun, affordable family outing, a trip to watch the Saints is well worth your time.

A Club Rooted in Local Identity

St Albans City Football Club has long been woven into the fabric of the local community, carrying the city's name with pride through generations of players, staff, and loyal fans. Like many clubs of its kind, it has weathered the ups and downs typical of non-league football, built on the dedication of volunteers, local businesses, and supporters who keep the club running season after season.

This sense of belonging is part of what makes the club special. It isn't just a football team — it's a community hub where neighbours become familiar faces on the terraces, and where the city's sporting heritage continues to be written in real time.

The Matchday Experience

There's a particular charm to matchday at a club like St Albans City. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming rather than overwhelming — perfect for first-time visitors, families, and those who simply want to enjoy football in a relaxed, friendly setting. Expect the classic sounds of non-league football: chatter among regulars, the occasional cheer rippling through the crowd, and the comforting smell of a matchday snack in hand.

Unlike the big stadiums, here you're often standing just metres from the pitch, close enough to feel genuinely part of the action. It's an experience that reminds you why football became the people's game in the first place — unpretentious, community-focused, and full of character.

Why It's Worth a Visit

  • A genuinely friendly, inclusive atmosphere that welcomes newcomers and families alike.
  • An easy, low-key way to get out and about while supporting a local institution.
  • A great alternative to big-league football, with an intimate, up-close view of the game.
  • A chance to connect with the wider St Albans community and meet fellow supporters.

For those exploring active, feel-good things to do around Hertfordshire, a matchday at St Albans City ticks every box: it's social, it's local, and it supports grassroots sport that benefits the whole community.

Get Involved

Fancy seeing it for yourself? Check the club's official fixtures to plan your visit, and consider making a regular outing of it. Supporting local football clubs like St Albans City helps keep community sport alive and thriving — and it's a wonderfully simple way to add a bit more active, local fun to your calendar.

posts.title: Sport at Herts: Free Sessions, Clubs and the Sports Village
posts.content:
If you are keen to train hard, experiment with a new activity, or simply build more movement into your everyday routine, the University of Hertfordshire offers lots of ways to stay active. From gyms and classes to clubs and social sport, there are options to suit different interests, fitness levels and schedules, and many facilities are based right on campus or just a short journey from where you live.

Two gyms to choose from
As a student you can work out at two fully equipped gyms: the Oval Gym on College Lane and the Hertfordshire Sports Village on the de Havilland campus. The Oval Gym is open 24 hours, giving you the flexibility to train whenever it fits around your lectures, placements and social life. At the Sports Village gym you will find resistance and cardio machines, a large free-weights area and a multi-use functional training rig, as well as two group exercise studios where you can take part in a range of classes. Whether you prefer focused solo sessions or the buzz of group exercise, there is a space that works for you.

More than a gym
The Sports Village is a full sports hub rather than just a fitness suite. Alongside the gym, it offers a 25m swimming pool for lane swimming and general use, a 12m climbing wall for bouldering and climbing sessions, indoor sports halls, squash courts and outdoor pitches. These facilities are open to students, staff and the wider community, which helps create a lively, welcoming atmosphere. If you like to mix up your training, membership also gives access to group classes such as Pilates, so you can balance strength, cardio and mobility in one place.

Join a club
HertSquad’s Athletic Union brings students together through sport, with 28 different sports clubs to choose from. It caters for everyone from elite athletes who want to compete at a high level, to complete beginners who simply want to try something new and make friends. More than 25 clubs regularly represent the University in national university leagues and competitions, so there are plenty of chances to train with a team, wear university colours and experience match days and tournaments.

Moving between campuses
Getting to training, matches or the gym is made easier by a regular free shuttle bus between College Lane and de Havilland. All you need to do is show your student ID when you get on. This means you can live on one campus, study on another and still make the most of facilities at both sites without worrying about extra travel costs.

Costs (check the official website)
Membership options, prices and discounts can change, so check the official Hertfordshire Sports Village and HertSquad websites for the latest information before you join or book.

Good for: regular gym users, swimmers, social and competitive club players, and anyone who would like a range of sport and fitness options in one convenient, student-friendly setting

posts.title: Try Something New: Free and Beginner-Friendly Sport
posts.content:
You don’t need to be super fit, fast or experienced to get started – these sessions are designed for complete beginners as well as regular players. Here are some easy, low‑pressure ways to try sport for free in Hertfordshire, make friends, and feel more confident being active.

Free Active sessions
HertSquad’s Active Students programme offers free, friendly and inclusive activities open to everyone, with no sign-up fees, no long-term commitment and no pressure to perform. You can just turn up when it suits you. The programme includes a wide range of sports, games and social fitness sessions across both campuses, running throughout the week so you can fit them around your timetable. Past sessions have included activities like archery, basketball and social running, and there’s usually a mix of indoor and outdoor options. Check the latest timetable to see what’s on this term and pick something that matches your energy level and interests.

Taster sessions before you commit
Free Club Sport taster sessions let you try any session on the Compete or Represent programmes before you decide whether to buy a membership. You can meet the team, chat to the coach or student leaders, and get a feel for the level of play. It’s a relaxed, no‑obligation way to see whether a club feels right for you, whether you’re returning to a sport you love or trying something completely new.

Free bikes
The Active Ride scheme offers free bike hire for 2 hours, available from early morning to late evening, with convenient pick-up and drop-off points across campus. It’s a fun, flexible way to explore Hatfield and the local area with a friend, get to know the campus, or build a bit of extra movement into your day between lectures. For full details on how to book and where to collect your bike, visit herts.

Tips for your first session

  • Go with a flatmate or coursemate so you’ve got a friendly face and someone to chat to on the way there.
  • Tell the organiser or session leader you’re new and, if relevant, that you haven’t done the activity before – they’ll expect beginners and can help you settle in.
  • Try a session twice before you decide if it’s for you; the first time can feel unfamiliar, but the second time usually feels more relaxed.
  • Arrive a few minutes early, say hello to the organiser and a couple of people near you, and let yourself take things at your own pace.

Good for: first-years, international students, anyone nervous about starting, anyone returning to exercise after a break, and anyone who wants to be active without pressure or judgment.

posts.title: Privacy and Cookies
posts.content:
This page explains the cookies and analytics technologies used when you visit Herts Active, a student fitness and wellbeing project website hosted on WordPress.com.

Last reviewed: 10 November 2026. Herts Active is a university project. It does not currently sell products, run advertising campaigns or operate its own user-tracking platform.

1. What are cookies?

Cookies are small files stored by a website in your browser. Similar technologies, such as tracking pixels and browser storage, can also be used to remember settings or measure how a website is used.

2. Essential WordPress.com cookies and technologies

Herts Active is hosted by WordPress.com. WordPress.com may use essential cookies or similar technologies to provide and protect website services, such as account sign-in, security, spam prevention, comments and other features you choose to use. These are provided and managed by the hosting platform rather than by a separate Herts Active tracking system.

The exact cookies set can depend on whether you are signed in to WordPress.com and which features you interact with. For the platform's current cookie details, see Automattic's Cookie Policy.

3. Website analytics: WordPress.com / Jetpack Stats

WordPress.com provides built-in Jetpack Stats on this site. It is already enabled by the hosting platform; Herts Active has not added Google Analytics or a separate analytics plugin. Stats help the project understand which pages and guides are being viewed so that content can be improved.

Jetpack Stats uses a small tracking pixel that loads in the visitor's browser. Depending on the activity and settings, it can record:

  • Post and page views.
  • Video plays for videos hosted by WordPress.com.
  • Clicks on links that lead away from the website.
  • Referring website addresses and search-engine terms.
  • Broad location information, such as country (and, where available in the service, region or city).

To produce these statistics, Automattic says the underlying data can include an IP address, WordPress.com user ID and username if the visitor is signed in, browser or device user-agent, the page visited, referring URL, event time, browser language and country code.

What the Herts Active team can see: the site owner sees summary statistics, such as total views, popular pages and traffic sources. WordPress.com states that information directly identifying a particular visitor, such as their IP address or WordPress.com account ID, is not visible to the site owner through Stats.

How long the underlying logs are kept: Automattic states that Stats logs containing visitor IP addresses and WordPress.com usernames, where available, are retained for 28 days and used to power the Stats feature. On the WordPress.com Free plan, the site dashboard provides a limited recent-history view of basic traffic statistics.

More information is available in the WordPress.com Stats documentation and the Jetpack privacy information.

4. Advertising and third-party analytics

Herts Active has not intentionally added Google Analytics, advertising pixels, remarketing tags or a separate marketing analytics service. The site is on the WordPress.com Free plan, so WordPress.com may display its own platform promotions or apply platform-level technologies under its own terms and privacy information.

When you follow a link to an external website, that website's own privacy and cookie practices apply. Herts Active does not control those external services.

5. Your choices and an important Free-plan limitation

WordPress.com provides a Cookie Consent block for block themes, but its banner has an Accept button and does not provide a Reject button. WordPress.com says a third-party consent plugin is needed for a visitor-facing reject option; installing third-party plugins is not available on this site's current Free plan.

WordPress.com also states that site owners cannot disable Jetpack Stats on the Free plan, and its hosted Stats service does not currently provide a site-level visitor opt-out control. For these reasons, Herts Active has not added an accept-only banner that could suggest visitors have a choice that the current hosting setup cannot fully honour.

You can use your browser's privacy and cookie controls or privacy extensions to restrict some cookies and tracking technologies. This may also affect sign-in, comments or other website features. Browser controls are not a substitute for a properly configured website-level consent or objection mechanism.

Project limitation: this page explains the current WordPress.com Free setup; it does not claim that the site has a full cookie preference centre or that every visitor can opt out of site analytics from within Herts Active. If the project later moves to a plan that supports a suitable consent-management tool, the team should configure and test an Accept / Reject / Settings workflow before adding optional analytics or marketing services.

6. Changes to this page

This page should be reviewed whenever the site adds a new embedded service, analytics tool, advertising feature, form provider or other technology that stores or accesses information on a visitor's device.

Useful references: UK Information Commissioner's Office guidance on storage and access technologies · WordPress.com Cookie Consent block documentation.

posts.title: Student Blog
posts.content:
Welcome to the Herts Active Student Blog!

Discover simple ways to stay active, eat healthier, improve your wellbeing and enjoy student life without spending too much money.

Whether you're a beginner or already enjoy fitness, we've got useful tips and ideas to help you live a healthier and happier student life.

Explore our latest articles, fitness tips and affordable activities around Hertfordshire!

University life can be exciting, but balancing lectures, assignments, part-time jobs and social activities can sometimes make it difficult to stay healthy.

Staying fit doesn't have to be expensive or time-consuming. Even small changes to your daily routine can make a big difference to your physical and mental wellbeing.

At Herts Active, we believe every student deserves the opportunity to enjoy a healthy and active lifestyle, regardless of their budget.

Here are some simple ways to stay fit while enjoying your university life!

Explore Your Local Parks 🌳

You don't need an expensive gym membership to stay active. Walking, jogging and cycling in local parks are great ways to keep your body moving.

Hertfordshire has many beautiful outdoor spaces where students can enjoy fresh air, exercise and spend time with friends.

Whether you prefer a morning walk or an evening jog, outdoor activities are a great way to stay active without spending money.

Student tip: Invite a friend to join you for a weekend walk and make fitness more enjoyable!

Try Free Home Workouts 💪

Busy with university assignments? Don't worry! You don't always need to visit a gym to stay fit.

Home workouts are a convenient and affordable way to exercise. You can use your bedroom, living room or any small available space.

Here are some beginner-friendly exercises:

  • Squats
  • Push-ups
  • Lunges
  • Planks
  • Jumping jacks

Start slowly and choose exercises that match your fitness level.

Student tip: Try a 15-minute home workout between your study sessions!

Eat Healthy on a Student Budget 🥗

Count your calories before you pick your food at the cafes . University of hertfordshire's cafe display all the calorie count which actually helps students to make the right and effective decision bassed on their BMI and their daily calorie count.

Moreover University of Hertfordshire's cafes provide vageterian and non-vageterian meals along with the options like fish , chicken , beef, egg and lots of fresh produce.

Student tip: Always mix match your meal thats how you can get your best meal at the cheapest rate.

Take Care of Your Mental Wellbeing 🧠

University life can sometimes become stressful because of assignments, exams, financial responsibilities and personal commitments.

Looking after your mental wellbeing is just as important as looking after your physical health.

Here are some simple ways to improve your wellbeing:

  • Get enough sleep every night.
  • Take regular breaks while studying.
  • Spend time with friends and family.
  • Enjoy outdoor activities.
  • Try meditation or relaxation exercises.
  • Talk to someone you trust when you feel stressed.

Remember, you don't have to deal with everything alone. Your university may also offer student wellbeing and support services.

Student tip: Give yourself some time to relax every day. Your wellbeing matters!

Explore Herts Active

Write for Herts Active

Are you a University of Hertfordshire student with a useful idea, experience or tip to share? We welcome article ideas about fitness, local places, student food, sport and wellbeing.

How student submissions work

  • Send an idea: Use the form to share your proposed topic and a short outline. You do not need a WordPress account to send an idea.
  • Editorial review: The Herts Active team reviews submissions and contacts you if the idea is suitable.
  • Draft your article: For accepted contributors, the team can send a WordPress invitation so you can write a draft using your own account.
  • Approval before publishing: An editor reviews the draft, checks links and images, and publishes it when ready. Sending a form does not automatically publish an article.

Before you submit

  • Share original writing and credit sources for facts or quotations.
  • Only submit photos you took yourself or have permission to use.
  • Do not include private health details or personal information about other people.
  • Keep advice respectful, inclusive and suitable for a student audience.

How to submit an idea

At the moment, Herts Active is using an editor-reviewed contributor process rather than open public publishing. Share your proposed topic and a short outline with the Herts Active project team through your agreed university or project communication channel. The editors can then review the idea and invite selected contributors to the site.

Want to write a full article? Once an idea is accepted, a site administrator can invite you to WordPress.com as a Contributor. You will use your own account to create a draft, and the Herts Active editors will review and publish it.

A public submission form can be added once the team chooses a shared inbox for submissions. The form should be tested in Jetpack → Forms before being advertised to visitors, so ideas reach the right people.

Creating a general WordPress.com account does not automatically give you permission to write for Herts Active. The site currently uses the Subscriber role for public registrations; Contributors must be invited by an administrator.

How contributor accounts work

Herts Active can invite selected students as WordPress.com Contributors. A Contributor can create and edit their own draft posts, but cannot publish them or upload media. An editor or site administrator reviews and publishes approved work. Each student uses their own WordPress.com login; passwords should never be shared.

This gives students a way to contribute without opening the website to unmoderated public publishing. The site owner can send invitations from Users → Add New User and choose the Contributor role.

posts.title: Parks and Walking

Discover Parks and Walking Routes in Hertfordshire

Looking for fresh air, peaceful surroundings or a way to stay active without spending much money?

Hertfordshire has plenty of green spaces and walking routes to explore. Discover places where University of Hertfordshire students can enjoy nature, walk with friends and take a break from studying.

Stanborough Park

Stanborough Park in Welwyn Garden City is a lovely place to enjoy the outdoors. With lakes, open green spaces and walking paths, it is ideal for a relaxing walk, spending time with friends or taking a break from university work. You can enjoy the natural surroundings without needing to join a gym.

Stanborough Park gives University of Hertfordshire students a chance to relax after lectures, reduce stress and improve their physical well-being.

Students can enjoy walking, watersports and picnics with friends, helping them stay active and balance university life with leisure.

Verulamium Park

Located in St Albans, Verulamium Park is a beautiful green space with a lake, open lawns and scenic walking paths. It's a great place for students to enjoy a peaceful walk, meet friends or take a break from busy university life

Take a relaxing stroll through Verulamium Park and enjoy its peaceful lake, open green spaces and beautiful surroundings. Whether you're walking alone or catching up with friends, it's a lovely way to spend time outdoors in St Albans.

Explore Local Walking Route

Walking is an easy and affordable way to stay active while exploring Hertfordshire. Whether you prefer a short stroll or a longer walk, local parks and nature trails offer opportunities to enjoy fresh air, discover new places and take a break from studying.

Hatfield to Ellenbrook Field

Ellenbrook Fields is a green open space near Hatfield, making it a useful option for students who want to spend time outdoors.

Enjoy a walk through the open landscape, get some fresh air and take a break from your university routine. Check the route and access conditions before setting off

Walking is an easy and affordable way to stay active while exploring Hertfordshire. Whether you prefer a short stroll or a longer walk, local parks and nature trails offer opportunities to enjoy fresh air, discover new places and take a break from studying.

Free and Budget-Friendly Activities

Staying active doesn't have to be expensive! Hertfordshire has outdoor spaces where students can enjoy walking, fresh air and time with friends without paying gym membership fees. Always check local travel costs, parking charges and any activity fees before visiting.

  • Enjoy a park walk : Explore local green spaces and walking paths.
  • Walk with friends : Make your daily walk more enjoyable by going with classmates.
  • Explore nature : Discover new places, take photographs and enjoy the outdoors.

Tips for a Safe and Enjoyable Walk

  • Wear comfortable shoes: Choose footwear suitable for the route.

  • Plan your route: Check the distance and directions before leaving.
  • Bring water: Stay hydrated, especially on longer walks.

posts.title: Gym and Fitness

Looking to stay active while studying at the University of Hertfordshire? This guide helps you explore gyms, fitness facilities and exercise opportunities around Hertfordshire.

Whether you prefer working out independently, joining a fitness class or exercising with friends, you can compare options and find activities that suit your interests and budget.

University of Hertfordshire Sports Village

The University of Hertfordshire Sports Village in Hatfield offers students opportunities to stay active and enjoy a range of sports and fitness activities.

It is a convenient option to explore if you want to exercise, improve your fitness or take part in activities alongside your studies. Check the official facilities, opening hours and membership prices before visiting.

Make time for your fitness alongside your studies and explore the facilities available at the Sports Village and check which activities and membership options suit your needs and student budget.

Local Gyms and Fitness Centres

Hertfordshire has a range of local gyms and fitness centres for students who want to stay active. Depending on your location and budget, you can explore options offering gym equipment, fitness classes and workout spaces. Before joining, compare membership prices, student discounts, facilities and travel costs to find the best option for you.

Affordable Fitness for Students

Staying fit as a student doesn't have to be expensive. Before paying for a gym membership, look for student discounts, introductory offers and pay-as-you-go options.

You can also save money by using outdoor fitness spaces, following free workout videos or exercising with friends. Compare the available options to find something that fits your budget and routine.

Tips for Staying Active at University

  • Set realistic fitness goals that fit around your studies.
  • Try different activities to find something you enjoy.
  • Exercise with friends to help you stay motivated.
  • Check gym opening hours and student discounts before visiting.

Your fitness journey doesn't have to be complicated or expensive. Explore the options around Hertfordshire, choose activities you enjoy and make time for your wellbeing alongside your studies. Every small step counts.

posts.content:
Discover Wellbeing in Hertfordshire

University life can be exciting, but balancing lectures, assignments and personal life can sometimes feel overwhelming. Taking time to look after your wellbeing is important. Hertfordshire offers parks, leisure facilities and activities where students can relax, stay active and take a break from their studies. This guide helps you explore options that support both physical and mental wellbeing

Swimming for Physical and Mental Wellbeing

Swimming is a great way to combine physical activity with relaxation. Swimming pools and leisure centres around Hertfordshire give students opportunities to exercise, build confidence and take a break from studying.

You can swim at your own pace and choose a session that suits your schedule. Check local facilities for opening times, admission prices and student discounts before visiting.

Make time for yourself! Swimming can be an enjoyable way to stay active, unwind and create a healthy balance between university work and personal time.

Yoga and Group Fitness Classes

Yoga and group fitness classes can provide opportunities for students to stay active, manage everyday stress and connect with others. Students in Hatfield and the surrounding area can explore classes offered by local leisure centres and fitness providers. Activities and prices vary by provider, so check current timetables, booking requirements and student discounts before attending.

Yoga and group fitness classes offer structured opportunities to exercise, develop healthy routines and take time away from academic responsibilities.

University Wellbeing Support

University life can bring academic and personal challenges. University of Hertfordshire students can explore the support services available through the university, including resources for mental wellbeing and guidance on accessing further support.

Visit the university's official website to find current services, eligibility information and contact details.

Explore university support

Outdoor Activities for Wellbeing

Spending time outdoors can provide a welcome break from academic responsibilities. Activities such as walking, cycling and exploring nature trails offer opportunities to stay active, enjoy fresh air and spend time with friends. Students can explore outdoor activities around Hertfordshire and choose options that suit their interests, fitness levels and budgets. Check local routes and access information before setting off.

Explore Hertfordshire’s countryside

Affordable Wellbeing Activities

Looking after your wellbeing does not have to be expensive. Students can explore free or low-cost activities around Hertfordshire, including walking, cycling, university activities and community events.

Taking regular breaks, spending time outdoors and connecting with others can help create a healthier balance between studying and personal life. Check activity details and any associated costs before attending.

  • Explore free activities organised by the university.
  • Look for student discounts on local activities.
  • Spend time outdoors when the weather permits.
  • Make time for hobbies and social activities alongside your studies.

Wellbeing looks different for everyone. Explore the options available around Hertfordshire, choose activities that suit your needs and make time for yourself alongside your university commitments. Small, consistent steps can help you build a healthier and more balanced student lifestyle.

posts.title: Walking in Hatfield
posts.content:
You do not need a car or a gym membership to stay active at Herts. Hatfield and the paths around College Lane and de Havilland have free walks for a free period, an evening wind-down or a weekend reset. Start here, then open each place page for detail.

What you can do here

  • Ellenbrook Fields — grassland and woodland beside de Havilland (watch for grazing cattle)
  • Roe Hill Park, Howe Dell Woods and Oxleys Wood — shorter walks in Hatfield
  • The Alban Way — traffic-free former railway path towards St Albans
  • Hatfield Park woodland walks — ticketed; check Hatfield House first
  • Longer days out — Stanborough Park, Sherrardspark Wood, Heartwood Forest or Panshanger Park

Getting there from campus

Ellenbrook Fields and the Alban Way are walkable from de Havilland; from College Lane use the shuttle or a short bus or bike hop. Town parks such as Roe Hill are a walk or short bus across Hatfield. For Welwyn Garden City woods and lakes, use Uno buses or the train.

Why students like it

Walking is free, flexible and easy with friends. Start with Ellenbrook Fields if you want something close; save Stanborough or Heartwood for a clear afternoon. Wear shoes that cope with mud, take water, and stick to marked paths.

posts.title: Hatfield Park
posts.content:
A SENSE OF PLACE

History

Deer parks were recorded at Hatfield by the 13th century, and Hatfield House was built for Robert Cecil in the early 17th century near the site of the Old Palace. The estate preserves medieval wood-pasture, including pollarded veteran trees and grazing land shaped over centuries, and an ancient oak associated with the young Princess Elizabeth hearing of her accession. These dates describe the historic estate, not the opening of todayâ€™s visitor park. The information available does not date when its current gardens, woodland trails, or visitor facilities were added.

MAKE THE MOST OF YOUR VISIT

Facilities

  • Formal gardensSeasonal estate gardens; check Hatfield House visitor information for opening dates.
  • Woodland and meadowEstate landscape with veteran oak, hornbeam and beech trees.
  • Deer herdMenil fallow deer live in the parkland.

Walking and running routes

The estate has three nature trails through the park and woodland; the longest passes veteran trees.

Trail access is seasonal and route lengths vary. Check the estate map and opening information before setting out.

Why this park may suit you

Choose Hatfield Park if you want a seasonal estate visit with gardens, woodland scenery, deer and three nature trails. The trails suit a scenic walk; the published information does not identify a dedicated running track.

BEFORE YOU SET OFF

posts.title: Ellenbrook Recreation Ground
posts.content:
Ellenbrook Recreation Ground on Ellenbrook Lane, Hatfield (AL10 9RW) is a local park and play area close to the Ellenbrook / de Havilland side of town. It is a practical spot for a short outdoor break, a kickabout or outdoor gym work when you do not have time for a longer trip to Stanborough or Verulamium.

What you can do here

  • Use the fenced playground (including climbing kit and swings)
  • Play informal football or basketball on the goals and half-court
  • Try the outdoor gym equipment
  • Sit outside between lectures or after the gym at nearby Sports Village

Getting there from campus

From de Havilland campus it is a short walk or bike ride along Ellenbrook Lane. From College Lane, take a bus towards Ellenbrook / St Albans Road or cycle via local roads — typically 10–20 minutes depending on mode. Street parking nearby is limited; walking or cycling is easiest.

Why students like it

It is free, local and low-pressure: useful for a quick reset without planning a full park day. Facilities are outdoor and weather-dependent, so it works best as a short visit rather than a destination trip.

Related posts

posts.title: Stanborough Park
posts.content:
Stanborough Park (Stanborough Lakes) on Stanborough Road, Welwyn Garden City (AL8 6DF) is a large lakeside park with two main lakes, trails, play areas and a watersports centre run by Better. At around 126 acres it is one of the best “big day out” green spaces near Hatfield.

What you can do here

  • Walk or run the lakeside paths and nature trails
  • Try watersports on the South Lake (sailing, kayaking, canoeing, paddleboarding when sessions run)
  • Hire rowing boats or pedalos on the North Lake in season
  • Use Splashlands and the play park in warmer months (seasonal)
  • Join Stanborough parkrun on Saturday mornings (free; check the event page)

Getting there from campus

Uno buses between Hatfield and Welwyn Garden City serve the Stanborough Road corridor; the park is also a short hop from Welwyn Garden City station by bus or bike. Pay-and-display parking is available and gets busy on sunny days. From College Lane allow roughly 20–35 minutes.

Why students like it

Lakes, long paths and optional watersports make it more interesting than a plain town park. Boat hire, open-water swim slots and café hours change by season — confirm on the Better Stanborough Park page before you go.

Related posts

posts.title: Oxleys Wood
posts.content:
Oxleys Wood is a small local woodland nature reserve in south Hatfield (about 1.3 hectares), managed by Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council. It is handy when you only have 30–45 minutes and want trees and a pond without leaving town.

What you can do here

  • Follow the circular trail through oak, ash, elm, willow and poplar woodland
  • Visit the pond and wetter northern area (paths can be muddy)
  • Watch common birds and insects in a compact urban nature site
  • Pair a short walk with nearby streets and allotments on the return loop

Getting there from campus

Access is from Deerswood Avenue in south Hatfield (opposite Badgers Way). From College Lane it is a short bus ride or a longer walk/cycle across town. There is no large visitor car park — arrive on foot or by bike where possible.

Why students like it

It is free, close and low-effort: a proper pocket of nature when a big country park feels too far. Parts flood after heavy rain, so wear sturdy shoes and check conditions via the council Oxleys Wood page if the weather has been wet.

Related posts

posts.title: Sherrardspark Wood
posts.content:
Sherrardspark Wood is an ancient oak and hornbeam woodland on the north-west edge of Welwyn Garden City. It is a Local Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest (around 80 hectares), so it is one of the best nearby places for a quiet, shady walk under mature trees.

What you can do here

  • Walk or jog on the network of footpaths and bridleways
  • Build a short family-friendly loop or a longer woodland circuit
  • Spot woodland birds and seasonal wildflowers
  • Combine a visit with Welwyn Garden City town centre afterwards

Getting there from campus

Travel to Welwyn Garden City by Uno bus or train from Hatfield, then walk into the wood from the town side or use the Rectory Road car park (often listed as free, 24-hour — confirm on the council site). From College Lane the journey is typically 25–40 minutes plus a walk into the trees.

Why students like it

It is free, peaceful and dense woodland — ideal when you want a screen break without paying for a park ticket. There is no café inside the wood, so bring water. For access notes see the Welwyn Hatfield Council Sherrardspark Wood page.

Related posts

posts.title: Panshanger Park
posts.content:
Panshanger Park is a large country park and nature reserve between Hertford and Welwyn Garden City, with lakes, wetlands, grassland and ancient trees. Managed with Tarmac and partners including Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, it is a strong choice for a longer weekend walk away from campus.

What you can do here

  • Follow waymarked trails such as the Oak Trail, Dragonfly Trail, Repton Trail and Ancient Tree Trail
  • See the Panshanger Great Oak and other veteran trees
  • Watch wildlife around the lakes and wetlands (stay on permissive paths; do not swim)
  • Picnic or take a longer circular walk across the parkland

Getting there from campus

Main car parks are on Panshanger Lane (SG14 2TS, entry typically 8am–5pm) and Thieves Lane (SG14 2WN). Parking is pay-and-display. By public transport, trains to Hertford North leave a walk of about 1 km; some buses on Welwyn Road stop north-east of the park. From College Lane allow a longer trip — check National Rail and local bus apps for the day’s best link.

Why students like it

It feels like countryside without going far from Herts: big skies, lakes and proper trail lengths. Rules change with management notices, so read the latest visitor guidance on the Panshanger Park visit page before you go.

Related posts

posts.title: King George V Playing Fields
posts.content:
King George V Playing Fields on Beehive Lane, Welwyn Garden City (AL7 4BP) is a multi-sport park run with Better. It packs playgrounds, courts, pitches and outdoor fitness into one free-to-enter site — useful when you want activity options beyond a simple walk.

What you can do here

  • Use basketball courts, the skate park and multi-use games area
  • Book family tennis courts or play on the football pitches when available
  • Try the outdoor gym equipment and join health walk sessions when advertised
  • Visit the children’s playground and floodlit bowls green
  • Stop at the pavilion for a tea or coffee when it is open

Getting there from campus

Go to Welwyn Garden City by Uno bus or train from Hatfield, then continue to Beehive Lane in the south of the town (bike or local bus). Free parking is listed on site. Expect around half an hour or more from College Lane depending on connections.

Why students like it

You get courts, a skate park and outdoor gym kit without a membership fee for casual park use. Pavilion and court booking hours vary — check the Better King George V page before you rely on indoor facilities.

Related posts

posts.title: Moneyhole Lane Playing Fields
posts.content:
Moneyhole Lane Playing Fields in Welwyn Garden City (Money Hole Lane / Sylvan Way, AL7 2RT) is a local authority sports and recreation site managed with Better. It is best known for grassroots football and a simple outdoor visit rather than a leisure-centre experience.

What you can do here

  • Watch or play community football — the site has full-size and mini soccer grass pitches (club bookings apply)
  • Use the children’s playground
  • Take the Tree Belt walk around the edge of the fields for a short outdoor break
  • Bring a ball or frisbee on open grass when pitches are not in use for matches

Getting there from campus

Travel to Welwyn Garden City by Uno bus or train from Hatfield, then continue by local bus or bike towards the Panshanger / Sylvan Way area on the east side of town. Free parking is listed on the Better site. Allow roughly 30–45 minutes door to door from College Lane without a car.

Why students like it

It is a no-frills, free outdoor space if you want fresh air, a kickabout or to support local youth football. Pitch hire and club use are organised separately — see the Better Moneyhole Lane page for facilities and notices.

Related posts

posts.title: Verulamium Park
posts.content:
Verulamium Park in St Albans is a free Green Flag park of about 100 acres on the site of Roman Verulamium. It is one of the best half-day wellbeing trips from Hatfield, with a lake, open grass, Roman remains and a museum beside the cathedral city.

What you can do here

  • Walk or run around the ornamental lake and parkland paths
  • See Roman city walls, the London Gate outline and the hypocaust mosaic (park entry is free)
  • Visit Verulamium Museum next door (museum tickets apply)
  • Use play areas and seasonal splash features when open
  • Join St Albans parkrun on Saturdays at 9am (free; register on parkrun.org.uk)

Getting there from campus

Bus from Hatfield to St Albans (Uno 602 is a common link), then walk or change for St Michael’s Village / Verulamium. St Albans Abbey station is about a 15-minute walk. Area address: St Michael’s Street, St Albans, AL3 4SW.

Why students like it

Free park entry, a scenic lake and Roman history make a proper day out without London prices. Check museum times on the St Albans Museums site before you travel.

Related posts

posts.title: The Oval Gym
posts.content:
The Oval Gym is the University of Hertfordshire’s 24-hour student and staff gym on the College Lane campus. With more than 50 stations, Matrix cardio kit and a free-weights area, it is the most convenient option if you live or study on College Lane and want to train around early lectures or late library sessions.

What you can do here

  • Use treadmills, bikes, rowers, climbers and other cardio machines with interactive screens
  • Lift with fixed resistance machines, cable stations, a Smith machine and dumbbells
  • Train at any hour — the gym is open 24 hours
  • Hire the outdoor MUGA for free as a UH student (check current booking rules)

Getting there from campus

You are already on site: The Oval is on College Lane. From de Havilland, use the university shuttle / Park and Ride or a short Uno bus hop. Watch the induction video before your first visit — details are on the Oval Gym page.

Why students like it

It is exclusive to UH students and staff, open round the clock, and right on College Lane, so you avoid a town trip. Access is included in Oval, Duo Gym and All Inclusive student memberships — check current prices and joining fees on sport.herts.ac.uk.

Related posts

posts.title: David Lloyd Hatfield
posts.content:
David Lloyd Hatfield is a large private health club at The Hangar, Hatfield Business Park (AL10 9AX), close to the de Havilland campus. The Grade II listed hangar setting is unusual, and the club packages gym, swimming, spa and racquets under one roof. It is a premium option compared with campus or budget gyms.

What you can do here

  • Use the gym, fitness classes and stretching areas
  • Swim in the heated 25 m indoor pool and 20 m outdoor pool
  • Play tennis on indoor and outdoor courts, plus badminton, padel and squash where offered
  • Use spa facilities such as the Himalayan salt sauna and steam room (membership-dependent)

Getting there from campus

From College Lane, head towards Hatfield Business Park / Mosquito Way — it is a short bus or bike ride towards de Havilland and the Hangar site. From de Havilland campus it is walkable for many students. Free on-site parking is listed by the club for members and visitors on a tour.

Why students like it

If you want pools, tennis and spa facilities in one membership near campus, this is the fullest offer in Hatfield. It is membership-based and more expensive than university gyms, so compare carefully. Check current membership types and prices on the David Lloyd Hatfield website before committing.

Related posts

posts.title: The Gym Group Welwyn Garden City
posts.content:
The Gym Group Welwyn Garden City is a 24-hour budget gym inside The Howard Centre shopping mall (Unit 29, AL8 6HA). It suits UH students who want flexible, no-contract training a short trip from Hatfield, especially if campus gyms feel busy or your timetable does not match Sports Village hours.

What you can do here

  • Train any time — the gym is open 24 hours, seven days a week
  • Use cardio kit, free weights, plate-loaded stations and a functional / HYROX-style area
  • Join free member classes when they are on the timetable
  • Use lockers, showers and free parking listed by the gym

Getting there from campus

Welwyn Garden City is roughly 7–8 km from College Lane. Uno buses towards Welwyn Garden City (for example the 653 corridor) stop near the town centre; the Howard Centre is a short walk from the bus station and train station. By bike or car the journey is about 15–20 minutes depending on traffic.

Why students like it

24-hour access and flexible memberships work well around lectures and part-time jobs. Prices and student offers change, so check current rates and any student saver codes on the Gym Group Welwyn Garden City page rather than relying on printed figures.

Related posts

posts.title: Hatfield Swim Centre
posts.content:
Hatfield Swim Centre on Lemsford Road is the town’s main public pool, run by Better. Use it for a swim, gym session or fitness class when you want an option beyond campus. It is a short walk from The Galleria and easy to reach from College Lane by bus or bike.

What you can do here

  • Swim in the unusual 33-metre main pool (depth changes across the lanes)
  • Use the learner pool, diving pool and health suite (sauna, steam and jacuzzi)
  • Train in the gym with cardio machines and free weights
  • Join classes such as aqua aerobics, Pilates, yoga, HIIT, group cycle and boxfit

Getting there from campus

From College Lane, take a local bus towards The Galleria / town centre and walk to Lemsford Road (AL10 0DH). Arriva 300 and 301 serve the area; Hatfield station is about 20 minutes on foot. Limited free parking is available — check signs on arrival.

Why students like it

You can combine a swim with shops and food at The Galleria. Pool and class times change, so check the timetable and prices on the Better Hatfield Swim Centre page before you go.

Related posts
