posts.title: Hello World!
posts.content: Welcome to WordPress! This is your first post. Edit or delete it to take the first step in your blogging journey.

posts.title: Parks and Green Spaces Near Hatfield
posts.content:
When you need a break from lectures and screens, Hatfield has some excellent green spaces within easy reach of both College Lane and de Havilland campuses. Here are three reliable options that work well for walks, runs or a quiet sit outside.

Ellenbrook Fields sits on the former Hatfield Aerodrome site, next to the de Havilland campus. It is a large public nature park with grassland, woodland and wetland habitats, plus permissive paths for walking and cycling. You will often see Longhorn cattle grazing in fenced areas — keep dogs on a lead near them. Parking is available at Notcutts Garden Centre, and bus routes along Hatfield Road / St Albans Road make it reachable without a car. It is free to enter and ideal for a long stroll or an easy run.

Stanborough Park is a short hop towards Welwyn Garden City (just off the A1(M) junction 4). This 126-acre park has two lakes, nature trails and lakeside paths. It is a good choice when you want a longer outing with somewhere to sit and take in the view. Pay-and-display parking is available; trains to Welwyn Garden City and local buses also serve the area.

Hatfield Park (the parkland around Hatfield House) offers marked woodland and park walks when it is open to visitors. Entry is ticketed for the gardens, park and woodland walks, so check opening times and prices on the Hatfield House website before you go. It is a calmer, more formal option than Ellenbrook Fields.

Quick tip: start with Ellenbrook Fields if you want something free and close to campus. Save Stanborough or Hatfield Park for a weekend when you have a bit more time. Always wear sensible shoes after rain — some paths get muddy.

posts.title: Campus Sports Facilities: Sports Village and the Oval Gym
posts.content:
You do not need an expensive town-centre gym membership to stay active at Herts. The university has two main on-campus options that students use every day.

Hertfordshire Sports Village is on the de Havilland campus (Hatfield Business Park, AL10 9EU). Facilities include a large gym (110+ stations), free weights, a multi-functional training rig, a 25-metre eight-lane pool, a 12-metre climbing wall, group-exercise studios, and tennis, squash and badminton courts. There are also outdoor pitches and a MUGA. The Sports Village is open to students, staff and the wider community. Student members should check current weekday access rules for the HSV gym and pool — at the time of writing, some membership types ask students to leave the HSV gym and pool by 5pm Monday to Friday.

The Oval Gym is on the College Lane campus. It is a 24-hour gym with 50+ stations, cardio and resistance machines, and a free-weights area. It is exclusively for University of Hertfordshire students and staff, which makes it handy for early-morning or late-evening sessions around your timetable. Students can also hire the MUGA at the Oval for free.

Memberships: student plans are sold through sport.herts.ac.uk and typically cover Oval-only, HSV, Duo Gym (both gyms) or All Inclusive options. Prices change with promotions, so check the student memberships page for the latest monthly and annual figures, joining fees, and what each plan includes. You will usually need proof of enrolment on your first visit, and a UK bank account for monthly Direct Debit plans.

Getting between campuses: if you train at the Sports Village from College Lane, use the university Park and Ride / shuttle where available, especially during chargeable parking hours on de Havilland.

posts.title: Budget-Friendly Ways to Stay Active at Herts
posts.content:
Staying active does not have to drain your student loan. Around Hatfield and St Albans there are plenty of low-cost or free options.

Walk for free. Ellenbrook Fields, Roe Hill Park, Howe Dell Woods and the Alban Way cost nothing to use. A 30–40 minute walk a few times a week is one of the simplest ways to protect your energy and mood during a busy term.

Try a local parkrun. Ellenbrook Fields parkrun used to run next to the de Havilland campus but no longer takes place. Nearby Saturday 9am options include Stanborough parkrun (Welwyn Garden City) and Oaklands College parkrun (St Albans). Register once on parkrun.org.uk, bring a printed barcode, and turn up — it is free, and you can walk, jog or run. Check the event page before you go in case of cancellations.

Use campus outdoor spaces. The Sports Village outdoor grounds and the College Lane MUGA / 3G pitch give you somewhere to kick a ball, do intervals or stretch without paying for a private pitch hire (check booking rules for the MUGA — students can often hire it free).

Join a student club or society. Herts SU sports clubs and recreational societies are usually cheaper than private gyms or town clubs, and they add a social side that helps if you are new to the area. Look on the Students’ Union site for current lists and trial sessions.

Home / hall workouts. Bodyweight sessions (squats, press-ups, planks, walking lunges) need no kit. Pair them with a short outdoor walk and you have a solid routine for exam weeks when the gym feels like too much effort.

Student tip: start small. Two free walks and one campus session a week beats an unused paid membership.

posts.title: Walking Routes Around Hatfield and St Albans
posts.content:
If you like a route with a clear start and finish, these paths are popular with Herts students and easy to fit around lectures.

The Alban Way is the standout option. It is an approximately 6.5-mile traffic-free walking and cycling trail along a former railway line between Hatfield and St Albans (part of National Cycle Network Route 61). The surface is mostly flat and paved, so it suits beginners, pushchairs and bikes. You can join it at points such as Ellenbrook Lane in Hatfield or Highfield Park in Fleetville, St Albans. Walking the full length takes roughly two hours one way; many students do a shorter out-and-back from the Hatfield end. Watch for wildlife in the verges, and look out for remnants of the old railway platforms in the undergrowth.

Ellenbrook Fields loops. From the de Havilland side you can build your own circular walk on the permissive paths through grassland and woodland. Distances are flexible — 20 minutes or well over an hour — and there are information boards about the site’s aerodrome history.

Stanborough Park lakeside paths. At Stanborough Park (Welwyn Garden City) you can combine shorter lake circuits (around 1–2.5 km options are signed) into a longer outing. Good when you want water views without travelling into London.

Practical notes: wear layers — Hertfordshire weather changes quickly. Take water, and on the Alban Way consider a bike light or reflective kit if you might finish near dusk. For public transport back from St Albans, check Intalink or National Rail rather than assuming a late bus.

Suggested first outing: Alban Way from the Hatfield end for 30–40 minutes out, then turn back. Easy, free, and a proper break from campus.

posts.title: Woodland Walks Near Hatfield: Heartwood Forest and Sherrardspark Wood
posts.content:
When you want trees, quiet paths and a proper break from campus, two of Hertfordshire’s best woodlands are within easy reach of Hatfield. Both are free to enter and work well for a weekend walk with friends.

Heartwood Forest

Heartwood Forest, near Sandridge north of St Albans, is managed by the Woodland Trust. At around 347 hectares it is one of England’s largest new native forests, with young woodland, ancient woods, meadows and wide views. Three waymarked trails start from the main car park: the Magical Meander (about 2.4 km), the Wildlife Wander (about 4 km) and the Heartwood Hike (about 4.3 km). Paths can get muddy after rain, so boots help. There are no toilets on site — the nearest public ones are in Sandridge — so plan ahead and bring water.

Sherrardspark Wood

Sherrardspark Wood sits on the north-west edge of Welwyn Garden City. It is an ancient oak and hornbeam woodland, a Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest. A network of footpaths and bridleways lets you build a short loop or a longer wander. You can reach it by train to Welwyn Garden City and walking in, or use the small car park off Rectory Road. There are no cafés inside the wood, which keeps it peaceful.

How to make a day of it

Start with Heartwood if you want signed trails and open views. Choose Sherrardspark if you prefer denser woodland closer to a train station. Stick to marked paths, take litter home, and check the Woodland Trust or Welwyn Hatfield Council pages before you go if the weather has been wet.

posts.title: A Day at Verulamium Park in St Albans
posts.content:
Verulamium Park is one of the easiest big green spaces to reach from Hatfield, and it rewards a half-day visit. Named after the Roman city of Verulamium, the park covers about 100 acres of parkland beside the River Ver, with Roman walls still visible and St Albans Cathedral nearby.

What you will find

The main feature is the ornamental lake, popular for a gentle circular walk of roughly 1.2 km around both lakes. There is an outdoor gym area, beach volleyball courts, a children’s play space and a café overlooking the park. Verulamium Museum sits at the edge of the park if you fancy a short cultural stop after your walk. Low-lying paths can flood after heavy rain, so check St Albans City and District Council updates if the weather has been wet.

Getting there from Hatfield

You can take a train or bus into St Albans and walk into the park, or drive and use pay parking at St Michael’s or Westminster Lodge. The Alban Way traffic-free path also links Hatfield with St Albans if you prefer to walk or cycle part of the way.

A simple student outing

Meet friends for a lakeside loop, pause on a bench with a packed lunch, then head into the city centre or catch a train home. It is free to walk the park itself. Opening times and any ticketed museum entry change, so check the Enjoy St Albans or council websites before you go.

posts.title: Exploring Panshanger Park: Trails, Lakes and Ancient Trees
posts.content:
Panshanger Park, between Hertford and Welwyn Garden City, is a large restored landscape of woodland, lakes and riverside paths. It is privately owned with permissive public access, so stay on the signed routes and follow the site rules.

Waymarked trails

Four waymarked walks make planning easy. The Oak Trail is about 2 km from the Panshanger Lane car park and leads to the famous Panshanger Great Oak. The Dragonfly Trail is about 3 km from Thieves Lane and loops around the lakes and River Mimram. The Repton Trail is about 4 km and follows the historic landscape views. The Ancient Tree Trail is about 6.5 km for a longer outing. Surfaces vary; expect mud in wet weather.

Practical tips

Car parks are at Panshanger Lane (SG14 2TS) and Thieves Lane (SG14 2WN). Parking charges apply — check the Panshanger Park website for current rates and opening times. Dogs are welcome but must be on leads around livestock and kept out of the lakes. Do not swim in the lakes or river. There are no litter bins, so take rubbish home.

Why students like it

It is ideal when you want more space than a town park: lakes for birdwatching, quiet woodland and room to walk and talk. You can also run on the permissive paths. Check panshangerpark.tarmac.com before you travel, as paths can close without notice.

posts.title: Comparing Hatfield Gyms for Students
posts.content:
Hatfield has several gym options, so it helps to match the venue to your timetable, budget and how far you want to travel from College Lane or de Havilland.

On campus first

The Oval Gym on College Lane is exclusively for University of Hertfordshire students and staff, with 24-hour access and 50+ stations. Hertfordshire Sports Village on the de Havilland campus has a larger gym (110+ stations), pool, climbing wall and studios. Student memberships are sold through sport.herts.ac.uk — plans typically cover Oval-only, HSV, Duo Gym or All Inclusive. Prices and weekday access rules change, so check the student memberships page and take proof of enrolment on your first visit.

Town options

PureGym Hatfield and NRG Gym Hatfield are 24-hour commercial gyms in town, useful if you live off campus or want a simple pay-monthly deal. Hatfield Leisure Centre (Better) has a gym, studios, sports hall and squash courts. Hatfield Swim Centre combines pool access with a gym if swimming is part of your routine. David Lloyd Hatfield and The Gym Group in Welwyn Garden City are further options if you have transport.

How to choose

Start with a campus tour or a day pass where offered. Ask about student rates, induction requirements and whether classes or a pool are included. Avoid signing a long contract until you have tried one or two sessions that fit your week. Always confirm current prices and opening hours on the venue’s own website.

posts.title: Your First Week at the Gym: A Beginner's Guide
posts.content:
Starting at the gym can feel intimidating, especially in the first week of term. A simple plan beats guessing what to do when you walk through the door.

Before you go

Book or complete an induction if your gym offers one — the Oval Gym and Hertfordshire Sports Village both expect new members to learn the basics safely. Wear trainers you can move in, take a water bottle and a small towel, and arrive with your student ID or membership details ready. If you are unsure about form, ask a member of staff rather than copying someone on the floor.

A gentle first-week structure

Aim for two or three short visits of 30–40 minutes. Warm up with five minutes of easy cardio, then pick a mix of machine or free-weight moves that cover legs, push, pull and core — for example squats or leg press, a chest or shoulder press, a row, and a plank. Finish with a short cool-down walk and stretches. Leave ego at the door: light weights with good form build confidence faster than heavy sets you cannot control.

Make it stick

Put sessions in your calendar like lectures. Go with a flatmate if that helps you turn up. Track what you did in the notes app on your phone so week two feels familiar. If anything hurts sharply, stop and seek advice. Check your gym’s website for class timetables if you prefer a guided session after the first few solo visits.

posts.title: Group Fitness Classes at Herts
posts.content:
If you struggle to stay motivated alone, group fitness classes give you a set time, a coach and a room full of people working at their own level. Hertfordshire Sports Village on the de Havilland campus runs a large class programme in two studios, and many student memberships include group exercise — confirm what your plan covers on sport.herts.ac.uk.

What to expect

Classes typically include strength, cardio, cycling and mind-body formats led by fitness professionals. Timetables change each term, so check the Sports Village site or app before you go. Arrive a few minutes early, introduce yourself to the instructor if you are new, and tell them about any injuries. You do not need to keep up with the fittest person in the room — modify moves and focus on finishing the session.

Other places to try

Hatfield Leisure Centre and Hatfield Swim Centre (both Better) also run studio classes such as Pilates, yoga and body conditioning. Commercial gyms in Hatfield may include classes in some memberships. Always check whether a class needs pre-booking and whether student rates apply.

A good starter approach

Book two different class types in your first fortnight so you can compare. Pair one class with one quiet gym or outdoor session. If a format feels wrong, switch — consistency matters more than finding the “perfect” class on day one.

posts.title: No-Kit Workouts for Halls and Shared Houses
posts.content:
Some weeks the gym is too far, too busy or simply not happening. A short bodyweight session in your room or kitchen still counts — and it needs no equipment.

A 20-minute room circuit

Do three rounds of: 10–15 squats, 8–12 press-ups (on your knees or against a wall if needed), 10 walking lunges per side, 20–30 second plank, and 30 seconds of marching or high knees. Rest for a minute between rounds. Keep the door clear so you have space, and use a towel or mat if the floor is hard. Open a window if you can — stuffy rooms make everything feel harder.

Pair it with outdoor movement

After the circuit, walk for 15–20 minutes around College Lane, Ellenbrook Fields, Roe Hill Park or Howe Dell Woods. Fresh air resets your head after a day of screens. If it is dark, stick to lit paths and go with a friend when you can.

Keep expectations realistic

Two or three of these sessions a week during exam season is a win. You do not need a perfect routine — you need something you will actually do. Save gym goals for quieter weeks, and use halls workouts to protect sleep, mood and energy when coursework peaks.

posts.title: Joining Herts SU Sports Clubs
posts.content:
Joining a university sports club is one of the fastest ways to stay active and meet people outside your course. At Herts, Club Sport sits under HertSquad and covers teams that train on campus and compete against other universities.

How joining usually works

Clubs are open to a range of abilities, not only experienced athletes. Look for free taster sessions at the start of term, then buy the relevant Club Sport membership through the booking system on sport.herts.ac.uk. Options typically include Represent (competitive university sport), Compete (recreational fixtures in sports such as badminton, basketball, table tennis and volleyball) and Performance for selected elite teams. Benefits and fees vary by sport, so read the current page before you pay.

What you get

Most Represent memberships include weekly coached training, use of campus facilities, competition entry and support for fixtures. Recreational Compete options are lighter and cheaper if you want regular play without a full league commitment. There is also a HertSquad Pass for discounted pay-as-you-play bookings.

Before you commit

Try a taster, check training times against your timetable, and ask the club about kit costs and travel to away fixtures. Societies listed on hertssu.com are a separate route if you prefer non-competitive activity. Always confirm dates, prices and eligibility on the official Herts Sport or Students’ Union sites.

posts.title: Swimming in Hatfield: Sports Village and Hatfield Swim Centre
posts.content:
Swimming is a low-impact way to stay fit between lectures, and Hatfield has two main indoor options students use regularly.

Hertfordshire Sports Village pool

The Sports Village on the de Havilland campus has a 25-metre, eight-lane deck-level pool. Student swim-only and wider memberships are available through sport.herts.ac.uk. Some gym memberships that include swim ask students to leave the HSV pool by late afternoon on weekdays — check the current access rules for your plan. Adult lessons are offered at extra cost. Book lanes or check the timetable before you travel across from College Lane.

Hatfield Swim Centre

Hatfield Swim Centre on Lemsford Road (run by Better) has a 33-metre main pool plus teaching and splash pools. It suits public lane swimming and lessons, and also has a gym and fitness classes on site. Opening times, session types and prices change, so use the Better website for the latest timetable and any student or concession rates.

Making it work as a student

Pack goggles and a padlock for lockers, and aim for off-peak slots if you can. If you are new to lane swimming, start in a slower lane and follow the pool etiquette signs. Never invent a training plan that ignores how you feel — short, regular swims beat rare marathon sessions.

posts.title: Five-a-Side and Campus Pitches at Herts
posts.content:
If football is your reset button, you do not always need a full eleven-a-side match. Campus pitches and the College Lane MUGA make it easy to organise a kickabout around lectures.

What is on campus

Hertfordshire Sports Village has outdoor grounds and new-generation astro pitches on the de Havilland campus. On College Lane, students can often hire the MUGA at the Oval for free — confirm the current booking rules at reception or on sport.herts.ac.uk. The Sports Village also supports Club Sport football and futsal pathways if you want structured training rather than casual games.

Organising a casual game

Message your flat or course group midweek, agree a 45–60 minute slot, and book the pitch or MUGA early in busy term weeks. Bring a pump, bibs if you have them, and water. Keep teams small for five-a-side so everyone touches the ball. Respect other users, clear rubbish, and leave on time if someone has the next booking.

Beyond campus

Hatfield Leisure Centre has 3G pitch hire for larger groups when campus slots are full. Prices and availability change, so check Better’s booking pages. Whether you play casually or join a club, the goal is the same: regular movement, fresh air and a reason to look up from your laptop.

posts.title: Climbing and Racquet Sports at the Sports Village
posts.content:
Beyond the gym floor, Hertfordshire Sports Village offers climbing and racquet sports that suit beginners and more experienced players alike. These are useful when you want a skill-based session instead of another machine circuit.

Climbing wall

The Sports Village has an impressive 12-metre wall with overhang, vertical and slab surfaces. Competent climbers can access the wall under the right membership; beginners should book an induction or taster. All Inclusive student memberships typically include climbing access and a taster session allowance — confirm details on sport.herts.ac.uk and the Sports Village climbing page. Never climb without the required competency check or staff guidance.

Tennis, squash and badminton

Match-quality courts are available for tennis, squash and badminton, including a dedicated badminton hall. All Inclusive members often get free off-peak court time when booked online; other users can hire courts. Equipment hire may be available if you do not own a racket. Check peak and off-peak definitions before you book.

How to start

Book a beginner session for climbing, or reserve a badminton court with a friend for a light first game. Wear clean non-marking trainers for indoor courts. If you enjoy it, look at Club Sport badminton or other racquet options for regular play. Always verify current prices, inductions and booking rules on the official site.

posts.title: parkrun Options Near Hatfield
posts.content:
parkrun is a free, timed 5k every Saturday morning. You can walk, jog or run, and a volunteer tail walker means nobody finishes last. It is one of the simplest ways for Herts students to build a weekend routine.

Important update

Ellenbrook Fields parkrun, which used to run next to the de Havilland campus, no longer takes place. Do not travel there expecting an event.

Nearby Saturday options

  • Stanborough parkrun — Stanborough Park, Welwyn Garden City (around AL8 6DF), Saturdays at 9:00. Multi-lap course on grass and trails near the lake; can be muddy when wet.
  • Oaklands College parkrun — Oaklands College St Albans Campus, Hatfield Road, AL4 0JA, Saturdays at 9:00. Mixed surfaces through the college grounds. Check the event page for any cancellations.
  • St Albans parkrun — Verulamium Park, Saturdays at 9:00. A popular parkland course close to the city centre.
  • Panshanger parkrun — Panshanger Park, Hertford, Saturdays at 9:00, starting near the Panshanger Lane entrance.

How to take part

Register once for free at parkrun.org.uk, print or save your barcode, and bring it every time. Check the event’s own parkrun page the night before in case of cancellation. Arrive a little early for the briefing, and volunteer when you can — the events only run because of volunteers.

posts.title: Managing Exam Stress with Movement
posts.content:
Exam season shrinks everything to revision timetables and late nights. Short bursts of movement will not finish your coursework for you, but they can calm your nervous system and improve focus when you sit back down.

Keep sessions short on purpose

Aim for 20–30 minutes rather than a heroic two-hour workout you will cancel. A brisk walk around Ellenbrook Fields, Roe Hill Park or the College Lane loop, a no-kit circuit in your room, or an easy swim all count. Put the session in your calendar between two revision blocks so it feels like part of the plan, not a distraction.

Use movement to interrupt spirals

When anxiety rises, change your environment: leave the library, walk for ten minutes without your phone podcast, then return with one clear next task. Pair this with basics you can control — water, a proper meal, and a fixed lights-out time most nights.

Know when to get extra help

If stress tips into feeling unable to cope, contact University of Hertfordshire Student Wellbeing via Ask Herts or email studentwellbeing@herts.ac.uk. For urgent support, use the university’s published 24/7 helpline details on the Ask Herts wellbeing pages. Movement helps many students, but it is not a substitute for professional support when you need it.

posts.title: University Wellbeing Support Services at Herts
posts.content:
Looking after your mental health is as important as looking after your timetable. The University of Hertfordshire provides dedicated Student Wellbeing services for enrolled students, and you do not need to wait for a crisis to use them.

What is available

Student Wellbeing can offer counselling, mental health advice, peer support and wellbeing activities, alongside accessibility and disability services. The team is based in the Hutton Hub on College Lane. You can find directions and contact details on Ask Herts — search for “Student Wellbeing” or “counselling and mental health support”.

How to get in touch

Request support through the Dean of Students enquiry routes on Ask Herts, selecting the counselling and mental health option where prompted. You can also email studentwellbeing@herts.ac.uk or call the published Student Wellbeing number on Ask Herts. For immediate wellbeing support, follow the university’s guidance on the Ask Herts “immediate wellbeing support” page, including the 24/7 helpline number listed there.

Alongside professional support

Friends, faith communities, sports clubs and simple outdoor time all help many students feel steadier day to day. Use the parks, gyms and walking guides on this site as everyday tools, and treat Student Wellbeing as the place to go when you need structured help. Always rely on Ask Herts for the latest phone numbers, opening hours and referral steps.

posts.title: Sleep and Routine Tips for Students
posts.content:
Sleep is the foundation of wellbeing, yet it is often the first thing to slip in halls. A few steady habits make lectures, training and mood easier to manage.

Protect a wind-down window

Pick a target lights-out time for most nights and protect the 30–45 minutes before it. Dim the main light, leave your phone charging across the room, and avoid starting a new episode or a long scroll. If your mind is busy, jot tomorrow’s top three tasks on paper so your brain does not rehearse them in bed.

Use daylight and movement

Morning light helps set your body clock. A short walk to campus, a loop of Milwards Park or a few minutes outside between lectures is enough. Regular activity — even gentle — improves sleep quality for many people, but finish hard workouts well before bedtime if they leave you wired.

Keep the basics boring

Caffeine late in the day, heavy late meals and irregular weekend sleep all disrupt the week that follows. Aim for a similar wake time even on Sundays when you can. If sleep problems persist for weeks, speak to a GP or contact Student Wellbeing via Ask Herts. Good sleep is a skill you practise, not a luxury you earn after deadlines.

posts.title: Making Friends Through Activity
posts.content:
Friendship at university rarely appears fully formed in a lecture theatre. Shared activity gives you repeated, low-pressure reasons to see the same people — which is how most student friendships actually start.

Choose repeating commitments

A weekly Club Sport training session, a Saturday parkrun, a regular badminton booking or a walking group beats one-off events. You do not need to be talented; you need to turn up. HertSquad clubs, SU societies on hertssu.com and casual campus pitch games are all useful starting points.

Start smaller than you think

Invite one flatmate to Stanborough parkrun, ask a seminar partner to walk the Alban Way, or join a beginner climbing induction at the Sports Village. Suggest a concrete time and place rather than “we should hang out sometime”. After the session, a simple “same again next week?” keeps the door open.

Balance social time and rest

You do not have to say yes to everything. Protect sleep and study blocks, and pick one or two activities that fit your values and energy. If loneliness feels heavy or persistent, Student Wellbeing on Ask Herts can help. Activity is a powerful way to meet people — and looking after yourself is part of being a good friend too.

posts.title: Our Story
posts.content:
ActiveHeartz started with a simple problem. When we arrived at the University of Hertfordshire, we wanted to stay active, but we had no idea where to go. Which gyms do student prices? Where can you go for a run that isn't next to a main road? Is there anywhere to play football if you're not on a team?

The answers were spread across dozens of websites, leaflets and word of mouth. So we decided to put them all in one place, written by students, for students.

Who we made it for

ActiveHeartz is for anyone studying at the University of Hertfordshire, whether you live on campus, in Hatfield, or commute in. We especially had these people in mind:

  • First-years who are new to the area and don't know where anything is yet
  • Students on a tight budget who need free or cheap ways to stay fit
  • International students looking for a friendly way to settle in and meet people
  • Beginners who feel nervous walking into a gym or joining a team
  • Busy students juggling lectures, part-time work and deadlines

How we organise the site

We grouped everything so you can find what you need in a couple of clicks. Choose a section from the menu, then pick a place to read our review.

Parks

Free green spaces and trails for walking, running and cycling.

Gyms

Student-friendly gyms, pools and leisure centres.

Sports

Team sports and casual sessions where you can make friends.

Classes

Yoga, group classes and support for your wellbeing.

Deals

Student discounts, pay-as-you-go and free activities.

Getting there

Every review explains how to reach the place from campus.

How we review places

Every review on ActiveHeartz follows the same simple format, so you can compare places easily:

  • What it's like: an honest overview of what to expect on your first visit
  • Star rating: we only recommend places we would happily send a friend to
  • Cost: free, pay-as-you-go or membership, so you know what fits your budget
  • Getting there: walking, cycling, shuttle or bus routes from College Lane and de Havilland

We keep our reviews positive and responsible. Our aim is to help you find somewhere great to get active, not to criticise local businesses.

Why it matters to us

Moving more is one of the easiest ways to feel better, both physically and mentally. A walk between lectures, a swim after a long day or a weekly game with friends can make student life less stressful and a lot more fun. We hope ActiveHeartz helps you find your thing.

You don't need to be experienced or super fit to start. Just pick one thing to try this week.

Team contribution:

Biwon and Mirab (Researchers and writers) - We were in charge of making the website's content all the information and researching them to see which could suit the students this includes all the reviews, gyms, activities and all the information was written by us.

Tayyab and Haris (Main website developers) - we were in charge of making the website from scratch this includes the pictures, headings, navigation system and overall giving the website a cleaner look so it can be easy to find the information which was written.

posts.title: Contact us
posts.content:
Get in touch

Hi! We're a small group of University of Hertfordshire students who put ActiveHeartz together because we know how hard it can be to find somewhere to get active when you're new to the area, short on time or short on money.

If you've got a question, spotted something we've got wrong, or there's a park, gym or club you love that we haven't covered yet, we'd genuinely like to hear from you. Here's how to get hold of us.

Things people often message us about

  • Suggesting a place for us to review
  • Updating opening times or prices that have changed
  • Asking which activity might suit them as a beginner
  • Telling us about a student deal we've missed

How to reach us

  • Leave a comment under any of our reviews and one of us will reply there
  • Tell us which place your message is about, so we can find it quickly
  • If you are suggesting somewhere new, let us know where it is and what you liked about it
  • Please don't share personal details like your phone number or address in a comment

We're students too, so we check messages around lectures. We'll do our best to reply within a few days.

Need support right now? We're not able to give medical or mental health advice. If you're struggling, the University's Student Wellbeing team is there for you, and in an emergency always call 999.

posts.title: Privacy Policy
posts.content:
Who we are
ActiveHeartz (https://activeheartz.blog) is a student project made by University of Hertfordshire students. It recommends places to stay active and look after your wellbeing near the University.

What information we collect
We only collect what is needed for the site to work:

  • Comments: if you leave a comment, we collect the name and email address you enter, plus your IP address to help stop spam.
  • Site statistics: WordPress.com collects anonymous visitor statistics, such as which pages are viewed, to help us improve the site.

We never sell your information or use it for advertising.

Cookies
When you first visit, our cookie banner asks for your consent. Non-essential cookies, like those used for visitor statistics, are only used once you accept.

  • Essential cookies keep the site working, e.g. remembering that you entered the page password.
  • Comment cookies (optional) can remember your name and email for next time. These last one year.

You can clear cookies at any time in your browser settings.

Images and links to other websites
Our photos are free stock images. Some reviews link to official websites, such as leisure centres. Those websites have their own privacy policies, and we are not responsible for how they use your data.

How long we keep your data
Comments are kept so we can reply to them and stop spam. You can ask us to remove your comment at any time.

Your rights
Under GDPR, you can ask to see the personal data we hold about you, or ask us to delete it. To do this, leave a comment on any review and we will get back to you.

Changes to this policy
We may update this policy as the site develops. The latest version will always be on this page.

posts.title: A Peaceful Walk at Ellenbrook Fields
posts.content:
Ellenbrook Fields is a large, open country park on the edge of Hatfield, just a short walk from the de Havilland campus. It’s perfect for clearing your head between lectures, with wide grassy paths, wildflower meadows and plenty of space to walk, jog or cycle.

It’s free to visit and great for all fitness levels, whether you want a relaxed stroll or a steady run. It also hosts a free weekly parkrun, a friendly way to meet people and stay consistent.

Review by: Ethan Williams

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
Advantage: Beautiful open views, quiet surroundings and plenty of space for outdoor activities.

Disadvantage: The paths can be slippery in winter, and there are few sheltered areas.

Overall: Ellenbrook Fields is a fantastic place to spend time outdoors. It offers a relaxing environment away from busy roads and is ideal for long walks, jogging and spending time with dogs. The open fields make it enjoyable for people of different fitness levels.

Good to know

  • There are several entrances, including one close to the de Havilland campus
  • Paths are mostly flat, so it suits all fitness levels
  • Look out for wildflowers and skylarks in spring and summer
  • Our top tip: go at sunset for amazing big-sky views

Reviewed by Tayyib

posts.title: Walk or Cycle the Alban Way
posts.content:
The Alban Way is a traffic-free path that follows an old railway line between Hatfield and St Albans. It is flat, easy to follow and passes close to the University, so you can start a walk, run or bike ride almost from your front door.

Why we recommend it

  • Flat and traffic-free, so it is great for beginners and cyclists
  • Surrounded by trees and nature, a calm break from studying
  • Links Hatfield to St Albans, so you can make it a day out

Quick info

  • Review by: Daniel Johnson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⯪(4.5/5)
  • Advantage: good connection between Hatfield and St Albans
  • Disadvantage: Limited parking and no public toilets directly on the trail.
  • Overall: Its good because mainly its free so wont affect students and it is suitable for different fitness levels.
  • Level: Beginner

Good to know

  • The surface is mostly smooth, so it works for bikes and walkers
  • There are several access points, so you can do as much or as little as you like
  • You will pass old railway features along the way
  • Our top tip: cycle to St Albans and reward yourself with lunch in town
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Lakeside Walks and Water Sports at Stanborough Park
posts.content:
Stanborough Park in Welwyn Garden City is built around two lakes. You can enjoy an easy lakeside walk or jog, or try something different on the water at the park's water sports centre.

Why we recommend it

  • Beautiful lakeside paths for walking and running
  • Water sports like sailing and paddleboarding to try something new
  • Lots of open space for picnics and relaxing with friends

Quick info

  • Review by: Noah Davies
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Plenty of green space, scenic lake views and areas to sit and relax
  • Disadvantage: Some areas can be noisy and crowded during busy periods.
    Overall: Stanborough Park is a nice place to escape from everyday life and enjoy some fresh air. The lakeside setting makes it a good location for relaxing walks, picnics and spending time outdoors.

Good to know

  • There are paths around both lakes, so you can choose a short or long loop
  • Water sports are seasonal, so check what is running before you go
  • It is a popular spot for families on sunny weekends
  • Our top tip: go on a weekday afternoon for a quieter lakeside walk
Water sports centre

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: A Run Around Historic Verulamium Park
posts.content:
Verulamium Park in St Albans is one of the most popular parks in Hertfordshire. Wide paths loop around a lake and across open fields, with Roman ruins along the way, making every run or walk feel like a mini adventure.

Why we recommend it

  • Big, open park with lots of easy loops for running
  • Lake views and Roman history make it interesting to explore
  • Cafés and St Albans city centre close by

Quick info

  • Review by: Oliver Thomas
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Spacious parkland, attractive river views and interesting historical landmarks.
  • Disadvantage: Some walking routes can be muddy and uneven after rainfall.
  • Overall: Verulamium Park is an enjoyable destination for anyone who likes exploring the outdoors. It has a great mix of open fields, wildlife and historical attractions, making every visit interesting.

Good to know

  • The park is close to St Albans city centre and its cafés
  • You can see Roman remains as you walk around
  • The lake loop is a popular running route
  • Our top tip: pair your run with a visit to the city centre market
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Gosling Sports Park: Something for Everyone
posts.content:
Gosling Sports Park in Welwyn Garden City is a large sports centre with a gym, an athletics track, courts and pitches. Whether you want to lift weights, play tennis or try something more adventurous, it is all in one place.

Why we recommend it

  • Huge range of sports and activities on one site
  • Modern gym with plenty of equipment
  • Great for groups of friends wanting to try new sports

Quick info

  • Review by: James Walker
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: A good variety of indoor and outdoor sports facilities, with activities for different skill levels.
  • Disadvantage: Booking certain activities can be difficult during busy periods, and some sessions may be expensive.
  • Overall: Gosling Sports Park is a useful place for people who enjoy staying fit and learning new skills. There are different activities to choose from, making it suitable for beginners as well as experienced sports players.

Good to know

  • There is a wide range of activities on one site
  • Some activities need booking, so plan ahead
  • There is parking on site if you are driving
  • Our top tip: check the timetable for quieter off-peak times
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Make a Splash at Hatfield Swim Centre
posts.content:
Hatfield Swim Centre is a modern pool and gym in Hatfield town. It is a convenient choice for students who want to swim laps, take it easy in the water or add a gym session to their week.

Why we recommend it

  • Clean, modern pool close to College Lane campus
  • Gym on site, so you can combine swimming and training
  • Flexible options with no long contract

Quick info

  • Review by: Lucas Harris
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Clean swimming pools, friendly atmosphere and a good choice of swimming sessions.
  • Disadvantage: Changing rooms can get busy, particularly during family swimming sessions.
  • Overall: Hatfield Swim Centre is an enjoyable place to spend time while keeping fit. It provides a good environment for practising swimming, building confidence in the water and learning new techniques.

Good to know

  • Lane sessions are usually split by speed
  • There is also a gym, so you can combine a swim with a workout
  • Off-peak times are usually calmer

posts.title: Hertfordshire Sports Village: Your Campus Gym
posts.content:
The Hertfordshire Sports Village is the University's own sports centre on the de Havilland campus. It has a gym, swimming pool, sports halls and even a climbing wall, all just a few minutes from your lectures.

Why we recommend it

  • On campus, so it fits easily around your timetable
  • Student memberships designed for UH students
  • Gym, pool, sports halls and a climbing wall in one place

Quick info

  • Review by: Harry Clarke
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: A wide range of sports facilities, fitness classes and opportunities to take part in team activities.
  • Disadvantage: The centre can feel busy at popular times, and finding parking may sometimes be difficult.
  • Overall: Hertfordshire Sports Village is a good destination for anyone looking to enjoy an active lifestyle. There are plenty of ways to exercise, improve sporting abilities and meet new people.

Good to know

  • It is on the de Havilland campus, so it is easy to fit in between lectures
  • There are student memberships just for UH students
  • Facilities include a gym, pool, sports halls and a climbing wall

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Westminster Lodge: Swim and Train in St Albans
posts.content:
Westminster Lodge Leisure Centre sits on the edge of Verulamium Park in St Albans. It has swimming pools, a gym and a busy timetable of fitness classes, so it is a great all-in-one stop for a workout.

Why we recommend it

  • Pools, gym and classes under one roof
  • Right next to Verulamium Park for a run before or after
  • Modern, welcoming facilities

Quick info

  • Review by: Jacob Hall
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: A welcoming leisure centre with swimming lessons, fitness facilities and activities for all ages.
  • Disadvantage: Some swimming sessions have limited spaces, so planning ahead is important.

Good to know

posts.title: Try Something New with Active Students
posts.content:
Active Students is the University of Hertfordshire's programme of casual sport and activity sessions. There is no pressure and no experience needed. You just turn up, have fun and meet new people.

Why we recommend it

  • A great way to try new sports without committing
  • Easy way to make friends, especially in your first year

Quick info

  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

posts.title: Smash It at Comets Badminton
posts.content:
Comets Badminton is a local club in Welwyn Hatfield. It is a fun, sociable way to improve your game and play regularly with others who love the sport.

Why we recommend it

  • Friendly club atmosphere
  • Regular games to keep you consistent
  • Good way to meet people outside of uni

Quick info

posts.title: Playing Football at the University
posts.content:
Football is one of the easiest ways to stay active and make friends at Herts. You can join a University team, play casually through student sessions, or book a pitch with friends for five-a-side.

Why we recommend it

Good to know

UH sport

posts.title: Move Your Body, Calm Your Mind
posts.content:
Exercise is not only about fitness. A short walk in a park, a gentle yoga class or a run with friends can lower stress and help you sleep and focus better, especially around deadlines.

Why we recommend it

  • A 20-minute walk in Ellenbrook Fields or along the Alban Way can clear your head
  • Group sessions help you feel less alone
  • The University offers active wellbeing sessions for students

Quick info

  • Review by: Thomas Roberts
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Encourages a healthier lifestyle through relaxation techniques, stress management and positive thinking.
  • Disadvantage: Mindfulness activities may take time to get used to, especially for students who are new to meditation.
  • Overall: Mental health and mindfulness at the University of Hertfordshire provide students with an opportunity to focus on their personal wellbeing. Taking part in these activities can help students understand their emotions, deal with everyday challenges and create better routines.

Good to know

  • Even short bursts of movement can lift your mood
  • Green spaces near campus are great for switching off
  • Moving with friends helps you feel more connected
  • Our top tip: schedule a short walk into every study day
Active Wellbeing

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Support from UH Student Wellbeing
posts.content:
If you are struggling, you do not have to deal with it alone. The University of Hertfordshire offers free, confidential wellbeing support for students, alongside activities that help you look after your mental health.

Why we recommend it

  • Free and confidential for UH students
  • Friendly staff who understand student life
  • Works well alongside staying active

Quick info

  • Review by: Jack Turner
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Helps students access advice, develop independence and find support when facing personal or academic difficulties.
  • Disadvantage: It can sometimes be difficult to know which support service is best for a particular problem.
  • Overall: The University of Hertfordshire’s student wellbeing support is a useful resource for students adjusting to university life. It gives students opportunities to discuss concerns, access helpful guidance and find ways to overcome challenges.

Good to know

  • Support is free and confidential for UH students
  • You can reach out about small worries as well as big ones
  • They can point you to other services if needed
  • Our top tip: save their contact details now, before you need them

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Find Your Calm with Yoga and Pilates
posts.content:
Yoga and Pilates are great for building strength, flexibility and focus. They are beginner friendly, low impact and a lovely way to switch off from studying.

Why we recommend it

  • Gentle on the body and good for posture after long study sessions
  • Classes available at the Hertfordshire Sports Village and local leisure centres
  • Helps reduce stress and improve sleep

Quick info

  • Review by: Leo Collins
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Encourages relaxation, strengthens core muscles and helps improve breathing and body awareness.
  • Disadvantage: Some classes require previous booking, and certain positions may take practice to master.
  • Overall: Yoga and Pilates offer a refreshing way to stay active without doing high-intensity exercise. They allow participants to work at their own pace while developing strength, improving posture and learning useful relaxation techniques.

Good to know

  • Classes suit all levels, including complete beginners
  • Great for posture after long study sessions
  • Helps with stress and sleep
  • Our top tip: tell the instructor if it is your first class
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Get Active for Free in Hertfordshire
posts.content:
You do not need money to get fit. Hertfordshire is full of free parks, trails and community events, perfect for students on a budget.

Why we recommend it

  • Free weekly parkrun 5k events across Hertfordshire
  • Free parks like Ellenbrook Fields and Verulamium Park
  • The Alban Way for free walking and cycling

Quick info

  • Review by: Ryan Morris
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Allows students to enjoy campus facilities, join community activities and discover new hobbies at little or no cost.
  • Disadvantage: The choice of free activities can vary throughout the academic year, so some opportunities may not always be available.
  • Overall: The free activities at the University of Hertfordshire are a useful way to make the most of student life. They give students the chance to explore different interests, become involved in campus life and spend time with others without needing a large budget.

Good to know

  • Parks and trails near campus are free all year round
  • Free parkrun events take place every weekend
  • No membership or equipment needed
  • Our top tip: invite a friend to keep each other motivated
Find a parkrun

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Pay As You Go: Train Without a Contract
posts.content:
Pay-as-you-go lets you use a gym or pool only when you want to, with no monthly fee. It is perfect if your timetable changes every week or you are still working out what you enjoy.

Why we recommend it

  • No long-term contract
  • Only pay for the sessions you use
  • Try different gyms before choosing one

Quick info

  • Review by: Adam Richardson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Easy access to different leisure activities, affordable single sessions and no long-term membership required.
  • Disadvantage: Prices can vary depending on the facility, and popular sessions may need to be booked in advance.
  • Overall: Pay-as-you-go options around the University of Hertfordshire are ideal for students who prefer having control over their spending. They make it easier to try different sports, attend fitness sessions and explore new activities without paying for a full membership.

Good to know

  • No contract or monthly commitment
  • Perfect for trying out different gyms
  • Can work out more expensive if you go very often
  • Our top tip: keep track of your visits for the first month
Find PAYG gyms

posts.title: Save Money with Student Discounts
posts.content:
Being a student comes with perks. Many gyms and sports centres near the University offer cheaper memberships for students, so always bring your student ID.

Why we recommend it

UH memberships

posts.title: An Easy 5k Run at Ellenbrook Fields
posts.content:
If you have been meaning to start running, Ellenbrook Fields is one of the easiest places near campus to do it. The wide, open paths mean you can find your own pace without dodging traffic or crowds.

What to expect

Expect long, gentle paths through grassland with big skies and very few hills. It is quiet on weekday mornings, and on weekends you will see other runners and dog walkers. After heavy rain some paths get muddy, so it feels more like a trail run.

Our tips

  • Wear shoes with a bit of grip in autumn and winter
  • There is not much shade, so bring water on warm days
  • Try a free weekend parkrun if you like running with others

Quick info

  • Review by: Amelia Brown
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Wide, flat paths with plenty of open space, ideal for walking, jogging and running.
  • Disadvantage: Some paths can become muddy after heavy rain, and there is limited shade on sunny days.
  • Overall: Ellenbrook Fields is a lovely, free outdoor space with peaceful scenery. It is great for beginners, regular runners and dog walkers.
  • Level: Beginner to intermediate

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: The Alban Way on a Grey Day
posts.content:
The Alban Way is lovely in the sunshine, but it is also a great option when the weather is not perfect. The trees along the old railway line give some shelter, and the flat route means you can keep moving without much effort.

What to expect

Expect a quiet, tree-lined path that feels calm even in drizzle. Some sections can collect puddles and leaves in autumn, so it is a little slower going. Bikes and walkers share the path, so it is friendly but you need to keep an eye out.

Our tips

  • Wear a waterproof and shoes you do not mind getting wet
  • Cyclists: ring your bell when passing walkers
  • Plan a short loop and turn back when you are ready

Quick info

  • Olivia Smith review:
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
  • Advantage: Flat, peaceful and surrounded by trees making it great for walking and cycling
  • Disadvantage: Some sections can become muddy in wet weather and walkers share the same path
  • Overall: The Alban Way is a lovely, free route which offers beautiful scenery also it is a great place to enjoy fresh air and exercise
  • Level: Beginner

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Trying Paddleboarding at Stanborough Park
posts.content:
If you fancy trying something completely new, the water sports centre at Stanborough Park is a fun place to start. Paddleboarding and sailing are great for balance and core strength, and they feel more like an adventure than a workout.

What to expect

Expect a short safety briefing before you get on the water, and probably a few wobbles at the start. The lake is calm and sheltered, which makes it beginner friendly. Sessions are seasonal and popular in summer, so it is worth checking times before you go.

Our tips

  • Book ahead in summer, especially at weekends
  • Bring a change of clothes and a towel
  • Go with a friend, it is much more fun when you both fall in!

Quick info

  • Review by: Sophia Taylor
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Lovely lakeside views, walking paths and plenty of outdoor activities.
  • Disadvantage: Can become busy at weekends, especially during warmer weather
  • Overall: Stanborough Park is a great place to enjoy the outdoors, with beautiful lakes and peaceful scenery. It is ideal for walking, cycling and spending time with friends or family.

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: A Weekend Day Out at Verulamium Park
posts.content:
Verulamium Park is perfect when you want exercise that does not feel like exercise. You can easily spend a whole afternoon walking around the lake, exploring the Roman remains and finishing in St Albans for food.

What to expect

Expect wide open lawns, a big lake with plenty of birds and lots of paths to explore. It gets busy on sunny weekends, which gives it a lively, friendly atmosphere. Cafés and the city centre are close by when you need a break.

Our tips

  • Combine a lake loop with a walk up into St Albans
  • Pack a picnic on warm days
  • Go early on weekends if you prefer it quieter

Quick info

  • Review by: Isabella Wilson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Beautiful historic surroundings, large green spaces and peaceful walking trails.
  • Disadvantage: Some areas can become crowded during weekends and holidays.
  • Overall: Verulamium Park is a wonderful place to explore, with a mixture of history, nature and open spaces. It is perfect for relaxing walks, picnics and outdoor activities.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Gosling Sports Park With Your Friends
posts.content:
Gosling Sports Park is a brilliant choice for a group day out. With so many activities on one site, everyone can find something they enjoy, from the gym to racket sports and the trampoline park.

What to expect

Expect a big, busy centre with lots going on. It is easy to fill a couple of hours trying different things. Some activities need booking, and the popular ones fill up at evenings and weekends.

Our tips

  • Book group activities in advance
  • Check the timetable for student-friendly times
  • Make it a social: plan food together afterwards

Quick info

  • Review by: Mia Robinson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Excellent sports facilities, spacious grounds and a wide range of activities.
  • Disadvantage: Some facilities can be busy during peak hours, especially after school and at weekends.
    Overall: Gosling Sports Park is a great place for keeping active and trying different sports. It offers plenty of opportunities for exercise, whether you enjoy swimming, tennis, athletics or using the gym.

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Swimming for Beginners at Hatfield Swim Centre
posts.content:
Not a confident swimmer? Hatfield Swim Centre is a relaxed place to build up your confidence in the water. Swimming is low impact and great for both fitness and stress relief.

What to expect

Expect lane swimming sessions split by speed, so you can stay in the slow lane without feeling rushed. Off-peak times tend to be calmer. The changing rooms are straightforward and the centre is easy to get to from Hatfield town.

Our tips

  • Start with short sessions and build up
  • Look for quieter off-peak times on the timetable
  • Ask reception about adult swimming lessons

Quick info

  • Advantage: Good swimming facilities, helpful staff and activities suitable for different ages.
  • Disadvantage: The pool can become crowded during evenings and weekends.
  • Overall: Hatfield Swim Centre is a great place to enjoy swimming and improve fitness. It offers a welcoming environment for beginners and more experienced swimmers.
  • Level: Beginner to advanced

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Your First Climb at the Sports Village
posts.content:
The climbing wall at the Hertfordshire Sports Village is one of the best-kept secrets on campus. Climbing works your whole body and your problem-solving skills at the same time, and it is really satisfying when you reach the top.

What to expect

Expect a friendly, supportive atmosphere where beginners are welcome. You will usually need an induction or taster session first so you learn the safety basics. After that, it is a fun way to spend an evening with friends.

Our tips

  • Ask about taster or induction sessions first
  • Wear comfortable clothes you can stretch in
  • Go with a friend so you can take turns

Quick info

  • Review by: Grace Martin
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Modern gym equipment, a large swimming pool and a variety of fitness and sports activities.
  • Disadvantage: Membership and activity costs can be quite expensive, especially for regular visitors.
  • Overall: Hertfordshire Sports Village is a great place for people who enjoy keeping fit and trying different activities. It offers a range of facilities, including swimming, gym workouts and sports sessions.
  • Level: Beginner friendly

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Fitness Classes at Westminster Lodge
posts.content:
Westminster Lodge has a busy timetable of fitness classes, which is great if you work out better with an instructor and a group. It is a good option if you live in or near St Albans.

What to expect

Expect energetic classes and a modern studio. Because it is popular, peak-time classes can fill up and the centre can feel busy in the evenings. Booking ahead makes it much easier.

Our tips

  • Book classes in advance, especially evenings
  • Arrive a few minutes early for your first class
  • Try a quieter daytime class if your timetable allows

Quick info

  • Review by: Charlotte Lewis
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
    Advantage:     Good swimming facilities, a well-equipped gym and a variety of fitness classes.
  • Disadvantage: The swimming pool and gym can become crowded during peak hours.
  • Overall: Westminster Lodge is a great leisure centre for people who want to stay active and improve their fitness. It offers a good combination of swimming, gym workouts and exercise classes.
  • Level: Beginner to intermediate

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Making Friends Through Active Students
posts.content:
Moving to university can feel lonely at first, and Active Students sessions are one of the easiest ways to meet people. The focus is on having fun, not on being good at sport.

What to expect

Expect relaxed, welcoming sessions where lots of people are trying something for the first time. You do not need any kit beyond comfortable clothes and trainers, and there is no pressure to come every week.

Our tips

  • Check the timetable and pick one session to try
  • Bring a flatmate if you feel nervous going alone
  • Try a sport you have never played before

Quick info

  • Review by: Ava Young
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: A welcoming leisure centre with swimming lessons, fitness facilities and activities for all ages.
  • Disadvantage: Some swimming sessions have limited spaces, so planning ahead is important.
  • Overall: Westminster Lodge is an enjoyable place to spend time and focus on personal fitness. It provides opportunities to learn new swimming skills, build confidence in the water and take part in regular exercise.

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Your First Night at Comets Badminton
posts.content:
Joining a club can feel a bit daunting, but Comets Badminton is a good step up if you already enjoy playing casually and want regular games.

What to expect

Expect friendly, competitive games with players of mixed ability. As a club, it suits people who can commit to coming regularly. It is worth contacting the club first to check times and whether there is a space for new players.

Our tips

  • Contact the club before your first visit
  • Bring non-marking indoor trainers
  • Be ready to play doubles with new people

Quick info

  • Review by: Lily Scott
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
  • Advantage: Fun badminton sessions, opportunities to improve skills and a great way to stay active.
  • Disadvantage: Courts can become busy during popular sessions, and booking ahead may be necessary.
  • Overall: Smash It at Comets Badminton is a great place for anyone who enjoys racket sports or wants to try something new. It provides an opportunity to practise techniques, improve coordination and enjoy friendly competition.
  • Level: Some experience helps

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: A Cheap Night Out: Badminton in Hatfield
posts.content:
Looking for something different to do with friends? Booking a badminton court at Hatfield Leisure Centre is cheap, social and a surprisingly good workout.

What to expect

Expect simple, well-kept courts that you can book by the hour. Split between friends, it is an affordable evening. Rackets and shuttlecocks may be available, but it is worth checking before you go.

Our tips

  • Split the court cost between four people
  • Check if you need to bring your own rackets
  • Book evening slots a few days ahead

Quick info

  • Review by: Chloe Baker
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: A fun way to improve fitness, practise badminton skills and enjoy friendly matches.
  • Disadvantage: Court availability can be limited during busy evenings and weekends.
  • Overall: Badminton in Hatfield is a great activity for people who enjoy sports and staying active. It helps improve speed, balance and coordination while providing an opportunity to meet other players.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Five-a-Side With Your Flatmates
posts.content:
You do not need to be on a team to enjoy football at uni. Booking a five-a-side pitch with flatmates is a great way to keep fit and bond at the same time.

What to expect

Expect fast, fun games where everyone gets plenty of touches of the ball. Evening slots are the most popular, so book in advance. It is casual, so mixed abilities are completely fine.

Our tips

  • Get a regular weekly slot so it becomes a habit
  • Split the pitch cost between everyone
  • Bring water and a spare top

Quick info

  • Review by: Ella Nelson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Large playing areas, opportunities to develop football skills and a great environment for team sports.
  • Disadvantage: Pitch availability can be limited, especially when university teams are training or playing matches.
  • Overall: Playing football at the University of Hertfordshire is a great way to stay active and enjoy being part of a team. It helps improve fitness, communication and teamwork while allowing players to develop their football abilities.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Beat Exam Stress With a 20-Minute Walk
posts.content:
When deadlines pile up, it is tempting to stay at your desk. But a short walk outside is one of the simplest ways to reset your mind, and you will often come back more focused.

What to expect

Expect to feel calmer and clearer after just 20 minutes. Places like Ellenbrook Fields and the Alban Way are close to campus and quiet enough to really switch off.

Our tips

  • Leave your headphones out for once and notice your surroundings
  • Walk with a friend and agree not to talk about exams
  • Make it a daily habit during revision season

Quick info

  • Review by: Freya Mitchell
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Provides a chance to relax, manage stress and develop positive habits through mindfulness activities.
  • Disadvantage: Finding time to attend sessions can be difficult alongside lectures, assignments and other university commitments.
  • Overall: Mental health and mindfulness activities at the University of Hertfordshire are a valuable way for students to take a break from busy university life. They encourage relaxation, self-awareness and a more positive mindset.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: When to Reach Out to Student Wellbeing
posts.content:
Lots of students wait until things feel really bad before asking for help. You do not need to. The University's Student Wellbeing team is there for small worries as well as big ones.

What to expect

Expect friendly, confidential support from people who understand student life. They can help you talk things through and point you towards other support if you need it.

Our tips

  • You can reach out about stress, homesickness or anything else
  • Look up Student Wellbeing on Ask Herts to find out how to get in touch
  • Combine support with small healthy habits, like a daily walk

Quick info

  • Review by: Ruby Philips
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Offers guidance, support services and activities that help students feel included and supported
  • Disadvantage: Some support services may have waiting times, particularly during busy academic periods.
  • Overall: Student wellbeing at the University of Hertfordshire plays an important role in helping students enjoy university life. The support available encourages students to look after themselves, build confidence and manage challenges both inside and outside the classroom.
  • Level: Open to all students

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Yoga for Complete Beginners
posts.content:
If you spend hours hunched over a laptop, yoga is a brilliant way to undo some of the stiffness. It is gentle, calming and suitable for any fitness level.

What to expect

Expect slow, guided movements and lots of focus on breathing. Instructors usually offer easier versions of each pose, so nobody is left behind. Do not worry if you cannot touch your toes, most people cannot at first!

Our tips

  • Tell the instructor it is your first class
  • Wear comfortable, stretchy clothes
  • Go regularly for a few weeks to really feel the difference

Quick info

  • Review by: Evie Parker
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Helps improve flexibility, balance and posture while reducing stress and building strength.
  • Disadvantage: Some exercises can be challenging for beginners, and classes may have limited spaces.
  • Overall: Yoga and Pilates are excellent activities for improving both physical and mental wellbeing. They provide a relaxing environment to focus on movement, breathing and strength. Taking part in regular sessions can help improve flexibility, reduce tension and develop better body control.
  • Level: Complete beginners

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Five Free Ways to Get Active This Week
posts.content:
Staying active does not have to cost anything. Here are five free ideas you can try around Hatfield this week.

What to expect

Expect fresh air, a bit of effort and zero cost. These ideas work whether you have ten minutes or a whole afternoon.

Our tips

  • Join a free weekend parkrun 5k
  • Walk or jog a loop of Ellenbrook Fields
  • Cycle part of the Alban Way
  • Do a bodyweight workout in a local park
  • Organise a kickabout with friends on a free pitch

Quick info

  • Review by: Hannah Edwards
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Plenty of opportunities to socialise, explore the campus and take part in activities without spending money.
  • Disadvantage: Some free activities are only available at certain times or during specific university events.
  • Overall: Free activities at the University of Hertfordshire are a great way for students to enjoy university life without worrying about extra costs. They provide opportunities to meet new people, discover new interests and take part in enjoyable experiences outside of lectures.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: Is Pay As You Go Right for You?
posts.content:
Pay-as-you-go is a great way to try gyms and pools without signing a contract. But depending on how often you go, it is not always the cheapest option.

What to expect

Expect total flexibility: you pay for each visit and there is nothing to cancel. If you end up going several times a week, a monthly membership may work out cheaper, so it is worth keeping track.

Our tips

  • Use pay-as-you-go to try a few places first
  • Count your visits after a month and compare costs
  • Look out for student or off-peak prices

Quick info

  • Review by: Jessica Cooper
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
  • Advantage: Flexible access to sports and fitness facilities without needing to commit to a monthly membership.
  • Disadvantage: Regular visits can become expensive, and some activities require additional booking fees.
  • Overall: Pay-as-you-go activities near the University of Hertfordshire are a convenient option for students who want to stay active while managing their budgets. They allow students to choose when they exercise and only pay for the sessions they attend.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: How to Get the Most From Student Discounts
posts.content:
Student discounts can save you a lot over a year, but only if you remember to use them. Here is how to make the most of them.

What to expect

Expect most local gyms and leisure centres to offer some kind of student or concession price. You will usually need to show proof that you are a student.

Our tips

  • Always carry your student ID
  • Ask about student prices before signing up anywhere
  • Look out for free trials and taster sessions at the start of term

Quick info

  • Review by: Megan Bailey
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Reduced membership prices, affordable fitness options and access to gym facilities at a lower cost for students.
  • Disadvantage: Some discounts may only apply to selected memberships or require valid student identification.
  • Overall: Student discounts at gyms near the University of Hertfordshire are a great way to make fitness more affordable. They allow students to access exercise equipment, fitness classes and other facilities while keeping their spending under control.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

posts.title: About
posts.content:
Making student wellbeing easier, more accessible and more affordable.

Welcome to Herts Wellbeing, your local guide to health, fitness and positive living across Hertfordshire.

Our aim is to encourage individuals, families and communities to lead healthier, happier and more active lives by making local wellbeing opportunities easier to discover.

We believe that wellbeing is about more than just physical fitness. It includes maintaining a healthy lifestyle, looking after mental wellbeing, staying active, enjoying the outdoors and building positive connections within the community.

Through Herts Wellbeing, we aim to bring together useful information about local gyms, sports facilities, parks, walking trails, community activities and wellbeing events, helping people discover opportunities to improve their everyday lives.

Our aim is to encourage students of all fitness levels to explore what's available around Hatfield, try something new and make physical activity part of everyday student life.

Facilities: Free on-site parking, more than 50 free classes a week, and a dedicated ladies-only area with ladies-only classes. Equipment covers cardio machines, free weights, resistance machines, a Powerplate and a mat area, plus changing rooms, showers and lockers.

3. The Gym Group Luton
Location: C1–C2 The Galaxy, Bridge Street, Luton, LU1 2NB (town centre)
Membership: Off-peak £20.99, Standard £24.99 and Ultimate £30.99 a month (£24.99 for the first month), each plus a £15 joining fee. There’s also a 12-month saver option at £339 upfront with no joining fee.
Opening hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
Facilities: Free classes, personal trainers, cardio machines and free weights. Ultimate adds multi-gym access, one free membership freeze, guest passes and free Fiit online workouts. One member review mentions paying for parking nearby, so check parking before joining.

4. Active Luton – Inspire: Luton Sports Village / Lewsey Sports Park
Location: Inspire: Luton Sports Village, Butterfield Green Road, LU2 8DD, or Lewsey Sports Park and Pool, Pastures Way, LU4 0PF
Membership:

  • Inspire multi-centre (Adult): £44.99 a month
  • Lewsey dual-centre (Adult): £30.99 a month
  • Student/Senior rates: £36 (Inspire) and £24.75 (Lewsey)
    Pay as you go: Adult gym sessions £10, after a required induction.
    Opening hours: Not 24/7. Check each centre’s timetable.
    Facilities: Over 200 classes a week across the centres with multi-centre membership. The multi-centre plan also lets you use Lewsey, Lea Manor, High Town Gym and Stockwood Athletics Centre, and there are women-only gym sessions. Lewsey has a 70-station gym with plenty of free parking.

posts.title: Gym in St Albans
posts.content:
1. PureGym St Albans
Location: Unit 3, Abbey View Retail Park, AL1 2RJ
Membership: Off-Peak £23.99, Core £30.99, or Plus £37.99 a month, plus a £15 joining fee
Opening hours: 24/7
Facilities: Gym over two floors, cardio and resistance machines, free weights, 50+ classes included, and free parking.

2. Everyone Active – Westminster Lodge Leisure Centre
Location: Holywell Hill, AL1 2DL, near Verulamium Park
Membership: Bundles from £26.99 a month, depending on what’s included. Day pass for £7.40 through Hussle.
Opening hours: Not 24/7. Check the centre's timetable.
Facilities: 200-station gym, swimming pool, sauna, steam room, fitness studios, climbing walls, hot yoga studio, and the Verulamium Spa.

3. Fitness First St. Albans
Location: Christopher Place Shopping Centre, St Albans City Centre
Membership: From £75 a month
Opening hours: Mon–Thu 5:30am–9:30pm, Fri 5:30am–8:30pm, Sat–Sun 7:30am–7:30pm
Facilities: Reformer Pilates, HYROX training area, recovery area, sauna, steam room, cold plunge, and free on-site parking.

posts.title: Gym in Borehamwood
posts.content:
1. PureGym Borehamwood
Location: The Point, 84 Shenley Road, WD6 1EH
Membership: Core £27.99 a month and Plus £34.99 a month, plus a £15 joining fee
Day pass: £6.99 through Hussle
Opening hours: Mon–Fri 6:30am–11pm, Sat–Sun 8am–10pm. It’s not 24/7.
Facilities: 160+ pieces of kit, brand-new equipment, Les Mills classes like Bodypump and Bodycombat. The nearest parking is Furzehill Road car park.

2. Anytime Fitness Borehamwood
Location: Unit 1CA, Borehamwood Shopping Park, WD6 4PR
Membership: Price not listed online, so enquire with the gym. Day pass £8.60 through Hussle.
Opening hours: 24/7. It’s the only 24/7 gym in town.
Facilities: 3 hours’ free parking, a 2-minute walk from Elstree and Borehamwood station, access to Anytime clubs worldwide, personal and small group training.

3. The Venue (InspireAll)
Location: 12 Elstree Way, Borehamwood
Membership: Monthly price not listed online, so check with InspireAll. Day pass £10, or Hussle Monthly+ £52.50.
Opening hours: Not 24/7. Check the centre’s timetable.
Facilities: Fitness studio with cardio and resistance kit, free weights area, swimming pool, sauna, steam room and personal training.
